Figures tab row gains a `<details open>` editor body via new `_buildFigureEditorBody(rootEl, fig)` — upload control (`PAPER_FIGURES.uploadImage` against the live yBlock attrs), caption Y.Text contenteditable bound through `bindYTextToContentEditable` with the paragraph render contract, layout grid (Width text input, Placement select, `\centering` checkbox, Alt text input). Tables tab row gains an analogous `_buildTableEditorBody(rootEl, tab)` — booktabs/header_row checkboxes, +Row/+Col buttons, per-column L/C/R alignment buttons (writes `attrs.align`), the grid editor itself with per-cell `<div.pe-grid-cell>` contenteditables, and the caption Y.Text editor. V3.125's reorder caveat fixed: new `_snapshotYValue(v)` recursively walks Y.Text / Y.Array / Y.Map / primitives into `{__ytype, value/items/entries}` snapshots; `_writeAttrValue(parent, key, snap, Y)` is the inverse hydrator using attach-then-mutate. `moveBlockWithinSection` rewritten to use these helpers — figure subfigures, table cells, table caption Y.Text, and skeleton_items now all survive a reorder lossless. The `Edit in panel ↗` link from V3.125 is the canonical edit entry on doc-side figure/table blocks. Equation blocks unchanged — LaTeX source is naturally inline-editable.)

V3.126 (Project Members assignment moved from Lab Notebook to Projects page — V3.118's admin Members modal is removed from `/rm/pages/lab-notebook.html`; the canonical assignment surface is now the per-item Members accordion on `/rm/pages/projects.html`. `projects.js` boots with a `_canonicalProjects: { itemId → {sourcePath, sourceKey, member_uids[]} }` map built by parallel-loading all four typed JSONs (`projects/papers.json`, `projects/courses.json`, `projects/infrastructure.json`, `projects/tools.json`) — each shards the same `projects` Firestore collection by `type`. New `renderMembersSection(item)` accordion appears immediately after Personnel, only for items whose id is mirrored in the canonical collection (silently no-ops on grants / conferences / library-only papers). `window.addProjectMember(itemId)` opens `openForm()` with a select dropdown filtered to `_roster` entries tagged `_firebaseUid: true` (legacy slug-id roster entries can't be resolved to Firebase auth so they don't grant access — they remain in Personnel for human attribution); on save it read-modify-writes the canonical typed JSON. `window.removeProjectMember(itemId, uid)` confirms before deleting the entry from `member_uids[]`. The Lab Notebook stays a read-only consumer of `member_uids[]` via the V3.118 `state.assignedProjectIds` derivation; the empty-state hint and a new admin variant both deep-link to the Projects page. The propagation invariant: any page that wants to gate a feature by project membership reads `member_uids[]` either via `api.load('projects/<type>.json')` or via a Firestore `collectionGroup('projects').where('member_uids','array-contains',uid)` query — today's consumers are PMR + Lab Notebook, future consumers (page-level access controls, project-scoped task views, project-scoped notebook search) inherit the same field with no schema migration. ALSO V3.125: Paper builder block management overhaul — section-bottom `+ Paragraph / + Equation / + Figure / + Table / + Reagent` toolbar retired in favor of an inline `+ Add` button rendered between every pair of blocks (and at top + bottom) inside each section. Clicking opens a popover menu (Paragraph / Equation / Figure / Table; Reagent/equipment for Methods sections) and inserts at exactly that position via new `insertBlockAt(sectionId, idx, kind, opts)` helper on `window.PaperEditor`. Equation choice opens the V3.124 panel-side creation modal pre-targeted to insert at the popped position; Figure/Table choices create a blank block AND open the side panel on the matching tab + scroll to the new row. Block reorder controls: each block toolbar gains `↑` / `↓` arrow buttons; the existing `⋮⋮` handle becomes a real HTML5 draggable supporting drop on another block in the same section to reorder. Both arrow + drag route through new `moveBlockWithinSection(sectionId, blockId, targetIdx)` (snapshot → delete → re-insert via attach-then-mutate, same shape as V3.115's section reorder). `moveBlockUp` / `moveBlockDown` / `moveBlockBefore` are convenience wrappers exposed on `PaperEditor`. Block-render ctx now carries `sectionId` so block-side controls can dispatch without re-walking sectionsArr. Doc-side figure and table block toolbars gain an `Edit in panel ↗` link button that calls `PaperEquations.showPanel()` + `setActiveTab('figures'/'tables')` + `scrollToFigureRow/scrollToTableRow(blockId)` — the inline editor stays for back-compat but the panel is the canonical surface. New panel APIs: `PaperEquations.setActiveTab(tabId)`, `scrollToFigureRow(blockId)`, `scrollToTableRow(blockId)`, `openEquationCreateModalAt(sectionId, idx)` (which stashes a `pendingInsertSectionId/Idx` in module state for the V3.124 modal's save handler to consume). Caveat: `moveBlockWithinSection` does best-effort attrs copy — primitive attrs survive but Y.Text / Y.Array / Y.Map sub-attrs (figure subfigures, table cells, table caption Y.Text) drop on reorder; deep-clone path is V3.126 work.)

V3.124 (Paper builder side-panel polish — three coupled tweaks to the V3.115/V3.120/V3.122 right slide-out: (1) **Resizable pane.** New `.pe-pane-resize-handle` on the left edge drives `_setupResize(panel)` to set width on `mousemove` (clamped to `[280, 800]`) and persist to `localStorage.rm_paper_pane_width` on `mouseup`. (2) **Unified equation creation in the panel.** V3.109 `+ New inline` button replaced with a single `+ Equation` button at the top of the Equations tab; opens a creation modal asking for Name + LaTeX + type radio (`inline` / `main`). New Y.Map field `type` on equation library entries. New "Main equations" panel section between Inline and Numbered; each main row has an `Insert as block` button that calls `PaperEditor.addEquationToSection(sectionId, {body, display: true, numbered: true, label})` to clone the LaTeX into a new numbered display block in the section of the last-focused paragraph (resolved via `_resolveSectionIdForInsert()` walking up `.pe-section[data-section-id]` ancestors). Section-level `+ Equation` button retired — the panel is the only equation creation surface. `addEquation(sectionId, opts)` extended to accept body/display/numbered/label so the panel-side flow can pre-populate. (3) **References tab UX.** Cited and Linked sections wrapped in `<details open>` collapsible elements with a custom `summary::after` chevron. The V3.122 read-only `unknown` badge for unknown-key citations replaced with a clickable red `+ Add to library` pill that opens a small modal (cite key pre-filled read-only, Title required, First author / Year / DOI optional); save creates a stub items.json entry with `meta.library.is_library_entry: true` + `stub_created_from_paper_builder: true`, then invalidates + reloads the citation index so the row flips to `cited` (green) within ~1 s. No new schema beyond the `type` field on equation library entries; no new Firestore paths.)

V3.123 (Lab Notebook DOE builder — Phase 2 of the ELN roadmap. New `🧮 DOE` toolbar button opens a 720 px modal with a design-type radio row (Latin Hypercube / Full Factorial / Central Composite), a factors editor (name / low / high / levels-for-factorial), per-type config (LHS run count; CCD center-point replicates with auto α = (2^k)^(1/4)), generate/preview/insert workflow. Algorithms in-house: `_doeFullFactorial` (cartesian product), `_doeLatinHypercube` (stratified-random with stratum-center sampling, no jitter — reproducible), `_doeCentralComposite` (2^k corners + 2k axial + n₀ centers). Run caps: 200 LHS, 256 factorial, 6 CCD factors — keeps the in-table preview readable and the entry doc well under 1 MB. Stored as structured `state.doc.design = {type, factors[{name,low,high,levels?}], runs[{factorName: value, ...}], config:{nRuns?,n0?,alpha?}, created_at}` — Phase 3 will overlay actuals onto each run without migration. New Design panel renders below the body and above the Protocols-followed panel; sticky-header monospace matrix table inside a max-height-320px scroll box; `✏️ Edit / Regenerate` + `⬇ Download CSV` (client-side Blob, named `<entryId>_<type>.csv`) + `Clear` actions. Schema: `notebookEmptyEntry` / `notebookHydrate` initialise/coerce `design`; `notebookIndexRow` exposes `design_runs` count for future rail-row signalling. No new Firestore rule, index, or Storage block — pure entry-doc field. ALSO V3.122: Paper builder References tab — closes the V3.115/V3.120/V3.122 plan. Replaces the placeholder References tab with three sections (Cited / Linked / Library search) plus a search input that filters the lab's full citation index. Each row renders a status badge (`cited` green / `linked` amber / `library` gray / `unknown` red), a deep-link title to `/rm/pages/library-paper.html`, author/year/journal meta, and per-row `Insert citation` + `Link to draft` / `Unlink` buttons. New `getCitedKeysInPaper()` walker traverses `paperMap.sections → children` for every `[@key]` token across paragraph bodies, V3.115 skeleton bullets, V3.102 figure captions, and V3.120 table-caption Y.Texts. `loadCitationIndex` projection extended with `linkedDrafts: lib.linked_drafts.slice() || []` so the panel filters "linked but not cited" without a second items.json fetch. `_toggleLinkToDraft` writes `meta.library.linked_drafts[]` via the standard `api.load`/`api.save` path (same as V3.106 reader-side picker), then invalidates + reloads the cached index so the row's status flips immediately. Lazy-load: first References-tab open triggers `loadCitationIndex()` and shows "Loading lab library…" placeholders; the listener on `paper-citations-loaded` re-renders when the index resolves. No new schema, no new Firestore paths.)

V3.121 (Lab Notebook GHS hazard warnings + location info on inventory chips — chip pipeline now stamps `data-inv-hazard-signal`, `data-inv-hazard-pictos`, `data-inv-locations`, `data-inv-storage` from the inventory record at insert; a sibling `<span class="ln-inv-hazard">` containing a Danger/Warning pill plus per-code GHS pictogram badges renders immediately after each chemical chip (`contenteditable=false`, sanitizer allowlists the new class + data attrs). The Materials panel becomes a two-line row layout (main: kind/name/meta/hazard, sub: 📍 location · 🌡 storage) with a graceful italic "📍 location not set" hint + an admin-only `(set)` link to `/rm/pages/inventory.html?focus=<id>` since 0/935 inventory items have populated `locations[]` today. New `openSafetyDetailsModal` shows the full SDS-style breakdown — H-codes, P-codes, exposure routes, PPE chips, NFPA 704 diamond (4-quadrant rotated CSS, blue/red/yellow/white), first-aid (inhalation/skin/eye/ingestion paragraphs), storage, locations, MSDS link — and reuses the V3.118 `.ln-modal-*` chrome unchanged. Picker popover row meta now shows the Danger/Warning pill + pictograms inline next to the name (highest-value placement: warning visible before pick) and a `📍 N location(s)` count when populated. `_projectInventoryEntry` projects the full safety record from `inventory/chemicals.json` plus `locations[]` from both inventory sources; `collectInventoryRefs()` derives `inventory_refs[]` from chip data attrs so the entry-level array stays in sync with the body. ALSO previous V3.121 — Protocols Builder Phase 3 — inventory linking on materials rows + inline `[!inv:<id>]` tokens in step / note / safety / figure-caption bodies. New `rm/js/protocol-inventory.js` (~270 lines) clones the lab-notebook V3.114 picker pattern: `ensureList()` loads + caches `inventory/items.json` + `inventory/chemicals.json`, dispatching a `protocol-inventory-loaded` document event on completion so bindings + materials cells re-render once the data arrives. `openPicker({onPick, anchorEl})` floats a search popover with ↑/↓/Enter/Esc keybinds, kind badges, and stock chips. `renderTextWithTokens(text)` substitutes `[!inv:<id>]` occurrences with chip spans. Materials block: each row's item cell has two modes — when `item_ref` is null, free-text `<input>` + `🧪` picker button; when set, a chip showing the item's display label + a colored stock chip + an unlink `×`. Picking auto-fills `free_text` so unlinking later still leaves human-readable text. Step / note / safety / figure-caption block controls gain a `🧪` button that opens the picker and inserts `[!inv:<id>]` at the end of the body Y.Text. `bindYTextWithVars` extended to substitute `[!inv:…]` tokens alongside V3.117's `[!var:…]` in a single sorted-by-offset pass. Stock chip is a 4-color severity scale (`full` green / `low` amber / `out` red / no chip otherwise). Tech debt: lab-notebook + paper-editor + this module are the three live copies of the inventory-picker pattern — flagged for a follow-on `rm/js/inventory-picker.js` extraction. ALSO V3.120: Paper builder pill-tab bar + global toolbar + Tables tab — V3.115 single panel-toggle button replaced with a persistent pill bar at the top of the editor (text-only Equations / Figures / Tables / References, no icons); active pill = active tab in the right slide-out, click again to close. Below the pills, a single global toolbar consolidates V3.107's per-paragraph rich-text buttons (B / I / X₂ / X² / `<>`) and the V3.109/V3.115 reference inserts (+ Eq / + Fig / + Table / + Cite). Each toolbar button uses `mousedown.preventDefault` to keep the focused contenteditable's selection across the click; reference buttons restore the saved caret before opening a picker. Tables tab fully wired: per-table row with Tab. N badge, schema readout (`3 × 4 · booktabs · header`), label/caption preview, Numbered checkbox, Insert reference / Open block actions. Table block toolbar gains Numbered + label + Tab. # badge mirroring V3.109/V3.115; below it a styling toolbar (booktabs / header row / per-column L/C/R alignment); below the grid, a caption contenteditable bound to a new `attrs.caption` Y.Text (idempotent migration from the legacy string). New `[!tab:<label>]` paragraph token renders as `Tab. N` chip and exports to `\ref{<label>}`. `tableToTex` rewritten to honor block-level attrs (`booktabs`, `header_row`, `align`, `numbered`, `label`) with template fallback. Per-paragraph rich-text toolbar (V3.107) retired; Cmd+B/I/E keybinds still work via `richTextKeydownHandler`.)

V3.119 (Protocols Builder Phase 5a — authorship, version control, forking. Every protocol carries an immutable `author_uid` + cached `author_name` set at creation; the editor topbar and list cards show the byline. New `rm/js/protocol-versions.js` (~280 lines) provides `saveVersion / listVersions / loadVersion / forkProtocol / migrateForkToStandalone`. "Save version" runs a Firestore transaction that increments `current_version` on the parent doc and writes an immutable snapshot to `protocols/{id}/versions/v{N}` with the dehydrated tree, meta snapshot, snapshotter uid + display name, optional label/message, and parent-version pointer. The historical-version viewer (`?version=N`) hydrates a LOCAL Y.Doc from the snapshot — same render code paths, no Firestore subscription, no edit affordances. Forks: any lab member can fork any protocol; `forkProtocol` does a transactional fork that creates a new top-level `protocols/{forkId}` owned by the forking user with `forked_from: {protocol_id, protocol_title, version, forked_at, forked_by_uid, migrated_to_standalone_at}` populated and atomically increments the source's `fork_count`. The fork-of chip displays lineage on both the editor (with link back to the parent) and list cards. "Migrate to standalone" stamps `forked_from.migrated_to_standalone_at` rather than nulling the field, preserving the lineage record while hiding the badge. Firestore rule `match /protocols/{protocolId}/versions/{vId}` — lab-member read or public read on parent's `status == 'published'`; only owner/admin create with `snapshot_by_uid == request.auth.uid`; immutable updates; admin delete only. Composite index `(forked_from.protocol_id asc, created_at desc)`. Schema bumped to `schema_version: 2`; legacy V3.113 docs default the new fields via `protocolHydrate`. ALSO V3.117: Protocols Builder Phase 2 — formulas with live variable propagation. New `rm/js/protocol-formulas.js` lazy-loads mathjs from CDN on first formula render and exposes a per-protocol symbol table built by walking every `formula` block. Inputs from `attrs.variables[]`; outputs from evaluating `attrs.expression` against the running scope (outputs of earlier formulas visible to later formulas — chained calculations work). Inline `[!var:<name>]` token in any step / note / safety / figure-caption body resolves to a `<span class="proto-var">value unit</span>` chip on blur; raw text is shown on focus so the literal token can be edited. Renderers refresh chips on a `protocol-vars-changed` document event without a full tree re-render. Schema for the new `formula` block: `{label, description, expression, variables: Y.Array<Y.Map<{name,label,default,unit}>>, output: Y.Map<{name,label,unit,decimals}>}`. mathjs-now-Pyodide-later per the user-locked roadmap; `python` block kind remains reserved for a later phase. Also: V3.113 polish — `canEdit` is consistently honored across all block renderers (read-only viewers see no controls and disabled inputs); seed-race guard ensures non-owners opening a brand-new protocol wait for the owner's first Yjs flush instead of double-seeding the tree. ALSO V3.116: Lab Notebook protocol references — new toolbar button `📋 Protocol` opens a search popover over the lab-shared `protocols` Firestore collection (sorted by `updated_at` desc, status badge per row); a click inserts a real `<a class="ln-protocol-chip" href="/rm/pages/protocols.html?protocol=<id>" data-protocol-id="..." data-protocol-title="...">📋 Title</a>` at the caret. Body sanitizer's `ALLOWED_ATTRS` extended for `A` to permit `class`, `contenteditable`, and `data-protocol-{id,title}`; the class attr is post-strip-restricted to the literal `ln-protocol-chip` and `contenteditable=false` is force-pinned. New entry-level `protocol_refs[]` array is fully derivable from chips in the body — `collectProtocolRefs()` runs after every keystroke and pre-save; chip deletion in prose flows back to the array automatically. Protocols-followed summary panel renders between the body and the materials panel; rail rows show a `📋 N` count alongside `📎 N` and `🧪 N`. The picker reuses the V3.114 `.ln-inv-popover` styling unchanged. No new Firestore rule, no new index, no new Storage block — the V3.113 lab-shared `protocols/list.json` route and the blanket `userData/{uid}/{document=**}` rule cover the read paths and the new field respectively. ALSO V3.115: paper builder tabbed right pane + Figures tab — V3.109 standalone Equations slide-out refactored into a four-tab pane (📐 Equations / 🖼 Figures / 📋 Tables / 📚 References), with the Equations tab carrying the existing inline-library + numbered-equations sections unchanged. Figures tab ships fully wired: per-figure thumbnail row with caption preview, label input, Numbered toggle, and a free-text subfigure chip editor (auto-letter A/B/C…). Right-click context menu in paragraph bodies extended to four items (added 🖼 Insert figure reference and 📚 Insert citation); the figure-reference picker is a two-step popover (figure with thumbnail → optional subfigure / range like `(A-C)`). Three new paragraph tokens — `[!fig:<label>]`, `[!fig:<label>:<panel>]`, `[!fig:<label>:<a>-<b>]` — render as `Fig. N`/`Fig. N (A)`/`Fig. N (A-B)` chips and export to `\ref{<label>}` with `\,(A)`/`\,(A--B)` suffixes. Figure block toolbar gains Numbered checkbox + label input + Fig. # badge mirroring the V3.109 equation pattern. Tables and References tabs render placeholder empty states until V3.116 / V3.117. Module symbol stays `window.PaperEquations` for back-compat; events fire on both `paper-equations-changed` (legacy) and `paper-panel-changed` (V3.115). No schema migration — pre-V3.115 figure blocks default to numbered=true with empty subfigures.)

## System Overview

McGheeLab website is a single-page application (SPA) using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses hash-based routing to navigate between sections without page reloads. Public site content is stored in content.json, while user-generated content (stories, profiles) lives in Firebase Firestore. Authentication is handled by Firebase Auth with invitation-based registration.

As of V3.40 the site is moving toward a **two-tier shape**: the public marketing SPA at `/` (mission, research, projects, team, classes, news, opportunities, login) and the auth-gated **RM** dashboard at `/rm/`. RM is the single home for every lab tool — the 12 standalone apps under `/apps/` and the public-site dashboard/admin/cv/guide routes are migrating into RM in three phases: **Phase A (V3.40)** stitches every existing lab app into RM via iframe-bridge wrappers and prunes the public **Lab Apps** menu; **Phase B (V3.41–V3.52)** ports each app onto the RM data contract (`api.load`/`api.save`, IndexedDB cache, `LIVE_SYNC`, `firebridge` auth gate); **Phase C (V3.53)** deletes `/apps/` and the public-site admin/dashboard surface entirely. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.40_rm_app_migration.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.40_rm_app_migration.md).

## Module Breakdown

### index.html
- **Purpose:** HTML shell with persistent header, navigation, hero, and footer
- **Key elements:** `#app` container swapped by router; three nav surfaces: `#desktop-nav` (inline horizontal, ≥768px), `#bottom-tabs` + `#more-sheet` (mobile tab bar, <768px), `#site-nav` drawer (legacy, hidden)
- **SEO:** Meta description, keywords, OpenGraph, and Twitter Card tags
- **User system nav:** Dashboard, CV Builder, Admin, Login/Logout links (conditionally visible based on auth state)
- **Script loading:** Firebase SDK (compat, including messaging) → Chart.js CDN → firebase-config.js → user-system.js → cv-builder.js → scheduler.js → class-builder.js → lab-apps.js → push-notifications.js → app.js (all deferred, in order); SW registration inline script at end of head
- **PWA:** Manifest link, theme-color, iOS PWA meta tags, favicon links, Microsoft Tile meta

### app.js
- **Purpose:** SPA router, page rendering, and UI interactions
- **Key functions:** Hash-based route matching with multi-segment support (`#/dashboard/story/:id`), dynamic content injection, expandable stories, mobile touch support
- **User system integration:** Routes for login, dashboard, cv, admin, logout, schedule; wires user-system page interactivity; appends Firestore stories to projects page; loads news feed from Firestore; hides hero on CV page
  - **Scheduler routes:** `#/dashboard/scheduler/{id}` (owner admin view), `#/schedule/{id}?key={uuid}` (private speaker access, key-only)
- **PI CV view:** `buildPiExpandedHTML()` renders collapsible `<details>` sections with filter bar, citation badges, year-sorted items; `wirePiCvFilter()` handles chip-based section filtering
- **News page:** `renderNews()` renders feed layout + filter-bar slot; `buildNewsFeedCard()` creates cards (now uses `buildExpandedHTML()` so team renders alongside sections); `wireNewsFeedInteractions()` hooks up social features using prefetched comment counts
  - **Filter bar:** `buildNewsFilterBar()` builds Type/Person/Time/Has-comments controls from loaded posts; `wireNewsFilters()` owns filter state and re-renders from the cached list via `applyNewsFilters()`; helpers `collectNewsPeople()` / `postInvolvesPerson()` unify author + team (author/mentor/contributors) for the Person filter
  - Comment counts prefetched once via `Promise.all(getCommentsByStory)`; stored on each post as `_commentCount` for instant has-comments filtering and badge rendering
- **Image lightbox:** `ensureLightbox()` lazily builds a single shared overlay in `<body>`; `openImageLightbox(src, alt)` opens it; `wireImageZoom(rootEl)` delegates clicks on images inside research-stories/news feeds. Supports wheel/double-click/pinch zoom and drag pan; closes on backdrop, X, or Escape
- **Error handling:** Render functions wrapped in try/catch with user-facing fallback messages
- **Router auth gate (V3.332):** `render()` short-circuits `dashboard`/`admin`/`cv`/`login` to `authLoadingHTML()` until `Auth._authStateResolved` is true; the `Auth.onChange` handler re-renders on first resolution (`lastAuthUid` starts `undefined` so a logged-out first resolution also fires). Kills the login-page flash on authenticated reloads. `apps` self-handles; `logout` stays reachable pre-resolution

### firebase-config.js
- **Purpose:** Firebase initialization with project credentials
- **Graceful degradation:** If credentials are placeholder values, logs a warning and skips init — site works without Firebase

### user-system.js
- **Purpose:** All user system logic — authentication, Firestore CRUD, image processing, dashboard, story editor, admin panel
- **Key sections:**
  - **Media utilities:** Client-side image resize via Canvas API → three webp resolutions (thumb 300px, medium 800px, full 1600px); video upload (mp4/webm, up to 50 MB) direct to Firebase Storage
  - **DB operations:** CRUD for users, stories, news posts, project packages, classes (course listings), invitations, comments, reactions collections
  - **CV-to-profile sync:** `syncCVToProfile()` maps CV builder data (journals, conferences, presentations, patents) to public user profile fields with year, citations, journal metadata, and other rich fields
  - **Auth:** Login (15s timeout via Promise.race), invitation-gated registration, Google popup login (15s timeout) with popup-blocked → `signInWithRedirect` fallback (`_ensureGuestDoc` shared by both paths; `getRedirectResult` return leg in `init()`), password reset (`sendPasswordReset` + inline Forgot-password flow with anti-enumeration copy), logout, auth state management (`_authStateResolved` flag — now consumed by app.js's router gate — `onChange`/`offChange` listener subscribe/unsubscribe), navigation updates, profile-load background retry (`_retryProfileLoad`, 3 attempts with backoff → dismissible `.profile-load-notice` banner; a null profile never drops auth), `friendlyAuthError()` error-code map (exported), `authLoadingHTML()` spinner placeholder (exported)
  - **Dashboard:** Profile editing (name, bio, photo, category), story list with create/edit/delete, scheduler management (create/list/delete, manage via scheduler editor)
  - **Scheduler editor:** `renderSchedulerEditor`/`wireSchedulerEditor` — admin/owner view of a scheduler using `McgheeLab.Scheduler` engine; `renderSchedulePage`/`wireSchedulePage` — private key-only speaker access
  - **Story editor:** Multi-section editor with text areas, drag-and-drop image/video upload, reorder/remove sections, live preview modal, save draft / publish / submit for review
  - **News editor:** Simplified story editor for news posts — title, category (Event/Conference/Paper/Highlight/Lab Life/Other), cover image, Team section (author readonly, mentor dropdown, contributor chip picker — mirrors story editor), sections with text + media, draft/publish flow. Saves `team: { author, mentor, contributors }` alongside legacy `authorName`/`authorUid`/`authorPhoto` for backwards compatibility
  - **Admin panel:** Tabbed interface — user management (role changes), invitation generator (with copy link), pending story review (approve/reject), pending news review (approve/reject), course listings (add creates both `classes` + `schedules` docs with auto-generated schedule ID; edit navigates to course builder; delete cascades across participants + classFiles + Storage + schedules)
- **Exports:** All render/wire functions and Auth/DB objects on `window.McgheeLab` namespace

### cv-builder.js
- **Purpose:** Full-featured academic CV builder — data management, import/export, analytics, AI assistant
- **Key sections:**
  - **Schemas:** 11 section types (profile, education, employment, journals, conferences, presentations, patents, grants, awards, teaching, service) with typed field definitions
  - **Parsers:** BibTeX (basic + context-aware filename detection), NSF Current & Pending, NSF Biosketch, duplicate detection
  - **Generators:** LaTeX (moderncv template), BibTeX export, PDF HTML (3 templates: classic, modern, NSF)
  - **External APIs:** CrossRef (DOI auto-fill, citation counts), ORCID (public works search), Anthropic (AI writing assistant via per-user API key)
  - **State management:** `_data` object stored in Firestore `cvData/{uid}`, auto-syncs associations to user profile on every save
  - **Versioning:** Named snapshots with per-section and per-entry visibility toggles
  - **Dashboard/Analytics:** Completeness stats, section counts, Chart.js charts (publications timeline, category breakdown)
- **Render/wire pattern:** `renderCV()` returns HTML shell; `wireCV()` loads data from Firestore, populates from user profile on first load, attaches all event listeners
- **Exports:** `McgheeLab.renderCV`, `McgheeLab.wireCV`

### scheduler.js
- **Purpose:** Standalone, reusable dual-mode scheduling engine — embeddable anywhere on the site (class pages, events, conferences). Zero module state; all state passed via config object.
- **Key sections:**
  - **Unified builder layout:** `builderHTML()` / `wireBuilder()` — calendar on left + scrollable day-column time grid on right; both modes share same layout; grid has one column per selected day with date headers + sticky headers; 7am–9pm, 15-min rows
  - **Two scheduling modes:**
    - **Sessions:** Admin sets session duration (15m–2hr) via dropdown, clicks grid cells to place/remove blocks of that length per day; `sessionBlocks: [{ id, day, start, end, color }]` — one block per day
    - **Freeform:** Click+drag to paint/erase individual cells per day; `freeformCells: ['2026-06-08-0900', ...]` — granular per-cell availability
  - **`sessionBlocks` / `freeformCells` data models:** `expandSchedule()` derives days + slots from sessionBlocks (supports both `sb.day` and legacy `sb.days`), falls back to `selectedDays` + `slotDefs`, then `startDate/endDate`
  - **Three role-based views:** Admin (setup + heatmap + guest management + optimization), Guest (availability input + submission form), Public (read-only grid + confirmed guests)
  - **View normalization:** `normalizeView()` maps legacy names (`speaker`→`guest`, `student`→`public`) for backward compat
  - **Admin view switcher:** Preview as Guest or Public
  - **Pure grid renderers:** `sessionsGridHTML()`, `freeformGridHTML()` return HTML strings; sessions grid marks invalid day+slot combos as disabled
  - **Drag-to-select:** `wireFreeformDrag()` — pointer events API for guest-facing freeform availability painting
  - **Optimization:** `optimizeSchedule()` — greedy constraint-based bipartite matching
  - **Setup form:** `setupFormHTML()` + `wireSetupForm()` — mode toggle; mounts unified builder; `builderApi` provides `.getBlocks()`, `.getCells()`, `.getDays()`, `.getDuration()` getters for save
  - **Configurable guest fields:** `guestFields` array toggles Talk Summary, Discussion Questions, Presentation Materials Link; empty = bare-bones availability only
  - **Custom yes/no questions:** `schedule.booleanQuestions: [{ id, text }]` — owner-defined boolean questions rendered as checkboxes in the guest Details card; answers stored as sparse map `participants/{key}.booleanAnswers: { [questionId]: true }` (only checked entries persisted, so deleted questions auto-clean). Stable `id`s preserve answers across text edits
  - **Callback-based persistence:** Scheduler never touches Firestore directly; host provides `onSaveSpeaker`, `onSaveSchedule`, `onAddSpeaker`, `onDeleteSpeaker`, `onRefresh`, `onSwitchView` callbacks
- **Public API:** `McgheeLab.Scheduler.render(config)` returns HTML; `McgheeLab.Scheduler.wire(containerId, config)` attaches listeners. Also exposes: `renderGrid`, `renderSetupForm`, `wireSetupForm`, `renderBuilder`, `wireBuilder`, `renderConfirmedSpeakers`, `expandSchedule`, `optimizeSchedule`, `heatColor`, `fmtTime`, `slotLabel`

### class-builder.js
- **Purpose:** Tab-based course builder with nested sections and widgets, autosave, admin preview, and role-based views. Consumes `McgheeLab.Scheduler` for the speakers section.
- **Key sections:**
  - **Section registry (`SECTION_REG`):** Maps 10 section keys to 4 component types — `text` (textarea editor), `files` (upload/download manager), `speakers` (delegates to Scheduler), `modules` (learning module manager)
  - **Widget registry (`WIDGET_REG`):** 7 widget types — text block, image (upload + caption), video (YouTube/Vimeo embed), link list, HTML embed, simulation (sandboxed iframe), divider
  - **Module state:** `_tabs`, `_activeTabId`, `_previewMode`, `_viewType`, `_classData`, `_speakers`, `_currentSpeaker`, `_useKeyAuth`, `_scheduleId`, `_dirty`, `_autosaveTimer`, `_fileData`
  - **Tab system:** `_tabs` array of `{ id, name, sections }` objects; tab bar UI with add/rename/delete; `switchTab()` gathers DOM content then swaps active tab
  - **Data model:** `tabs: [{ id, name, sections: [{ key, id, name, collapsed, content, storagePath, widgets: [{ kind, id, ...content }] }] }]`; sections are repeatable instances of a type; each stores its own content/name; widgets nested inside sections
  - **Repeatable sections:** Any section type can be added multiple times; no uniqueness constraint; each instance has independent name/content/collapse state
  - **Collapsible sections:** `collapsed` boolean on each section; toggle button (▶/▼) in chrome bar and readonly header; `toggleSectionCollapse()` updates DOM in-place; `.cb-collapsed` CSS class hides content
  - **Section naming:** Each section has a custom `name` (prompted on creation); double-click label to rename in admin mode; type badge shows SECTION_REG label
  - **Section type styling:** `.cb-section-type-{key}` CSS class on every section; default colored left borders per type (simulations=#4fc3f7, overview=#81c784, etc.)
  - **Per-section content:** Text sections store content in `section.content` (not `_classData`); file sections use `section.storagePath` for unique Firestore paths; `_fileData` keyed by `section.id`
  - **Migration:** `migrateLegacy()` converts old formats into tabs; `ensureSectionFields()` populates `name`, `collapsed`, `content`, `storagePath` from legacy data
  - **Preview toggle:** `_previewMode` flag; `isEditing()` helper used by all renderers; "Preview" button in header switches between editing and read-only views; preview banner shown
  - **Canvas layout:** `buildCanvasHTML()` renders tab bar + "Add Section" dropdown + sections with nested widgets; no side palettes
  - **Section renderers:** `buildSectionBlockHTML(section)` renders chrome bar with collapse toggle + collapsible wrapper containing `renderSectionBody()` + nested widgets + "Add Widget" dropdown
  - **Widget renderers:** `buildWidgetBlockHTML(widget, sectionId)` renders mini chrome bar + `renderWidgetBody()` nested inside parent section
  - **Tab management:** `addTab()`, `deleteTab()`, `renameTab()`, `switchTab()` — cannot delete last tab; rename via double-click → prompt
  - **Section management:** `addSection()` (prompts for name), `removeSection()`, `moveSection()`, `reorderSection()`, `renameSection()`, `toggleSectionCollapse()` — operate on active tab; DnD for reordering via handle
  - **Widget management:** `addWidget(sectionId, kind)`, `removeWidget()`, `moveWidget()` — up/down arrow buttons for reordering within a section
  - **Drag and Drop:** HTML5 DnD API for section reordering within canvas; handle-based activation; drop indicator between sections
  - **Autosave:** `markDirty()` sets flag + status indicator; `startAutosave()` runs 30s interval; `persistAll()` gathers content from DOM → saves `tabs` array (with all section content) to Firestore; `stopAutosave()` fires final save on leave; `beforeunload` warning
  - **Content gathering:** `gatherContentFromDOM()` reads textareas/inputs from DOM; section text via `.cb-section-text[data-section-id]`; uses `findWidgetById()` and `findSectionById()` for lookups
  - **Speakers component:** `buildSchedulerConfig()` constructs config object with ScheduleDB callbacks; delegates to `McgheeLab.Scheduler.render()` / `.wire()`; each speakers section gets unique container ID
  - **Settings modal:** Title, subtitle, semester, level, description, classDates, registrationLink fields
  - **ScheduleDB:** Firestore CRUD for `schedules`, `participants`, `classFiles` collections
  - **Default schedule seed:** BME 295C (sessions mode, Summer 2026, June 8–12, sections: overview + speakers + files)
  - **Persistence:** `tabs` array in schedule doc; `sections` array derived for backwards compat; text content stored per-section within tabs; `modules` array saved alongside tabs
  - **Learning modules:** `renderModulesBody(editing, section)` — **per-section since V3.716**. Admin view (reorder/title/file/homework/published cards) and public view (numbered card links to `#/classes/{classId}/modules/{mod.id}`), both reading `modulesForSection(section.id)` rather than the class-wide array, so each section numbers from 1 and holds only its own lessons. `wireModuleEditors()` handles add/delete/reorder — add carries `data-section-id`, and reorder swaps `order` only among the moved entry's own siblings. `buildHomeworkDropdown()` populates from `hasDue` file sections; `gatherContentFromDOM()` reads module fields; `persistAll()` includes `modules[]`.
    - **Placement helpers:** `modulesSections()` (every section of key `modules`, in tab order), `ensureModulePlacements()` (the migration/repair — adopts unassigned or orphaned entries into the first modules section; never `markDirty()`, so it rides along on the next real save and there is no migration script; bails on classes with no modules section), `modulesForSection(sectionId)`. Called from `refreshCanvas()` and once after `_tabs = migrateLegacy(schedule)`.
    - **Module viewer route:** `#/classes/{classId}/modules/{placementId}`. `wireModuleViewer(classId, modRef)` resolves **id first, filename second**, so pre-V3.716 bookmarks, `teacher-classes.js`'s list and `hw466ModuleHref` all still land; file *and* folder come from the resolved placement. This replaced a `findIndex(m => m.htmlFile === …)` first-match lookup that made two placements of the same basename one page served from the wrong folder — `modules/manifest.json` holds seven files named `overview.html`. `app.js` passes the route segment through opaquely and needed no change.
    - **Module types (V3.803):** one optional field `type` on each `modules[]` entry — `module` (default, every older entry), `pretest`, `homework`, `homework_key`, `report`, `test`; notes never carry one. An untyped entry reads as `guessModuleType(htmlFile, title)` (keyword rules, most specific first; `moduleType()` falls back to it) and `ensureModuleTypes()` stamps that guess at load so it shows in the editor and persists on the next save; the Add Module picker prefills Type from the picked file. `moduleHomeKey(mod)` maps a type to the `typedModules` section that LISTS it (`homeworkModules` "Homework & Keys", `reportTestModules` "Reports & Tests") or null (stays in its stack). Those sections are derived lists over `modulesForTypedSection(key)` (stack order: section tab order, then `order`), rendered by `renderTypedModulesBody`; the stack still owns add/reorder/retype/delete, and the public stack drops listed entries (`!moduleHomeKey(m)`) while the pretest is badged and unnumbered. `ensureTypedModuleTabs()` runs right after `ensureModulePlacements()` (load + every refresh; in-memory; never `markDirty()`; bails with no modules section) and creates the missing section: Homework & Keys joins the existing Homeworks tab (`findHomeworkTab()`: the `hwList466` tab, else a tab named like one) or a new public "Homeworks" tab; Reports & Tests is a new public tab after Homeworks, else before the first gated tab. Keys and tests start hidden (`MODULE_TYPE_HIDDEN_DEFAULT`). The viewer and `module-header.js` walk prev/next within the LIST the student came from (listed entries among their list in tab order; the stack skipping listed entries) and label progress by `moduleProgressLabel` / `progressLabel`. Guarded by section 7 of `scripts/tests/module-placements.test.mjs`.
    - **Still class-wide, by scope decision:** `whiteboard` sections (one board set per class), legacy same-key `files` sections (`storagePath = reg.path`), and `speakers`. Same class of defect, each with its own migration story — see `CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.716_module_section_instances.md`.
- **Render/wire pattern:** `renderClassPage(scheduleId)` returns HTML shell; `wireClassPage(scheduleId)` loads data, migrates legacy format, builds canvas with tabs, wires DnD + autosave
- **Teacher-class dispatch (V3.304):** immediately after `resolveSchedule`, docs with `kind:'teacher-class'` short-circuit to `McgheeLab.wireTeacherClassPage(scheduleId, schedule)` — the tabs/widgets engine never runs for external teacher classes. `wireModuleViewer` similarly soft-gates teacher-class modules via `McgheeLab.tcCanViewModules` (enrolled student / owning teacher / admin), replacing the iframe with a join prompt otherwise.
- **Exports:** `McgheeLab.renderClassPage`, `McgheeLab.wireClassPage`, `McgheeLab.ScheduleDB`

### Board families + student boards (V3.685)
- **Three families under a schedule, all sharing one engine and one doc shape. WHICH collection is the whole access model:** `whiteboards` (instructor's live class board — world-read, class-admin write), `notesBoards` (a student's learning-module notes — owner write; owner + `sharedWithUids` + staff read), `hwBoards` (homework working-out — owner + staff only). `mountBoardView({collection, ...})`; `BOARD_COLLECTIONS` allow-lists the name.
- **Ownership is proven from the doc id.** Board ids are `{key}_{uid}` (`ownerBoardId()` strips `_` from the key), so rules authorise with `boardId.split('_')[1] == request.auth.uid` — no document read, and it works **before the board exists**, which matters because a student's first visit reads a board nobody has created yet (with a uid *field*, `resource` would be null and the read would fail closed instead of returning "not found"). Same reasoning as `hwProgress`. It also solves the subcollection cost problem: `strokes`/`items` re-state the same id split, so the owner path costs zero extra reads; only a shared reader pays a `get()` of the parent.
- **`hwBoards` has no sharing clause anywhere** — "homework can never be shared with a classmate" is a property of the rules file, not a flag a client could flip. `scripts/tests/whiteboard-rules.test.mjs` proves it adversarially: a classmate *named in* `sharedWithUids` on a homework board still cannot read the board, its strokes, or its items.
- **`computeCanDraw()`** replaces the class-admin-only gate: class-admin for `whiteboards`, plain ownership (checked the same way the rules check it) for personal boards. Boards are created lazily on first open by their owner.
- **Opt-in classmate directory** — `directoryOptIn/{uid}` (student-written, closed key set) → staff presses **Publish class directory** (`hw466PublishDirectory`) → `directory/optedIn`, a names-only doc readable by signed-in `@arizona.edu` accounts. Needed because the roster is instructor-only (FERPA) and students cannot query `users`; nobody who has not opted in ever appears.
- **Export** — `exportBoardPNGs()` flattens pages off-screen through the *same* `paintBackgroundInto` + `paintStroke` used live, so an export is what the student drew. The homework modules fold it into the results payload they already download (schemas `bme466-hw0-v2` / `bme466-hw1-v3`, importers accept both, checksum salt untouched). Deliberately not a second download: the single blob→`a.download`→`a.click()` path is the only one that survives the viewer sandbox (V3.682).
- ⚠️ **Rules-authoring lesson baked in here:** `isAdmin()` dereferences `users/{uid}` unguarded and therefore RAISES for a signed-in user with no users doc — and a raising rule denies the whole expression. Leading with it locked a delegated class admin out of their own board; bme466's `ownerUid: null` raised on the next branch too (`.get(f, default)` returns a stored null, not the default). `wbClassAdmin()` now puts cheap non-raising checks first, guards the admin lookup with `exists()`, and guards the ownerUid compare with `is string`. Any new gate in an `||` chain must be **total**.

### whiteboard-core mount API + module panel (V3.684)
- **Why:** the board was a document-level singleton — one module-level `S` plus 20 hardcoded `getElementById('wb-*')` lookups over 11 ids — so it could exist once, in one DOM shape. Teaching from a laptop-projected module while writing on a tablet needs the board *inside* the module page, i.e. a second mount.
- **`Whiteboard.mountBoardView(rootEl, opts)`** — `opts:{classId, boardId, projector, chrome:'full'|'panel'|'none', view:{enabled}, items:{enabled}}` → handle `{destroy, getBoard, getPage, isAdmin, zoomBy, zoomFit, getView, addImageItem}`. Element resolution goes through `resolveEls(root)` → `S.els` → `el(key)`; `EL_SELECTORS` is the single map. `wireWhiteboardPage` is now a thin adapter owning the two host-only concerns: `document.body.wb-projector` and hashchange teardown. `Whiteboard.boardShellHTML(opts)` builds the markup for both mounts (`ids:true` only for the page route, whose CSS still targets `#wb-canvas-*`).
- **`S` remains one board per DOCUMENT** — not a limitation in practice (the panel lives in the module iframe, a different document) and re-mounting warns loudly rather than silently fighting over the canvas.
- **Viewer-local lens** — `S.view={tx,ty,scale}` in board-width units, applied only at paint time by `applyViewTransform`. `lensActive()` gates every transform call, so `view.enabled:false` mounts (page route, projector) never call `setTransform` — the projector-parity invariant is structural, not arithmetic. `normPoint` applies the inverse; `ERASE_TOL`/`MIN_SEG` divide by `viewScale()` so eraser size and sampling stay screen-relative. Persisted to `localStorage` per class+board — it must never reach Firestore.
- **Image items** — `…/whiteboards/{boardId}/items/{itemId}` `{pageId,type,x,y,w,ar,z,url,fullUrl,storagePath,src,srcLabel,srcModule,…}`, a **sibling of `strokes`** because images mutate per drag commit and strokes are the latency-critical feed. Rendered as DOM under the ink canvas (annotation composites on top). Its rules block restates the class-admin gate in full — rules do not cascade into subcollections. Storage is NOT the gate: bytes live under the broad `classes/{classId}/**` rule, but an image is only visible if an item doc points at it, and only class admins write those.
- **`modules/shared/whiteboard-panel.js` + `.css`** — the panel: context-panel geometry ported from `hw-00-pretest.html`, `[Live class board]`/`[My notes]` tabs (notes is an honest R2 stub, not a fake surface), live-board discovery via the schedule doc's `liveWhiteboard`, and canvas snap. It loads the **same** `firebase-config.js` the SPA does (no second config to drift) plus a ~20-line `McgheeLab.Auth` shim, because `user-system.js` is 263 KB of site chrome a module must not load. **No auth handshake is needed**: Firebase persists per-origin under the default app and the iframe is same-origin, so the parent's session is already there — which is also why the snap uploads and writes directly instead of proxying through the parent, and why it works on a direct link.
- **`whiteboard-board.css`** — board-view styles shared by `index.html` and the module panel, extracted from `styles.css` (which module iframes never load) so one stylesheet serves both mounts.
- **Class context:** `?class={classId}` on the iframe src and on direct "Open module" links. Nothing set it before, so an embedded module had no class context at all. `<meta name="ml-module-viewport">` opts a module into the viewport-height iframe regime alongside `#rail` — required for `position:fixed` panels, and detected by meta rather than element-sniffing because deferred scripts build the panel after the iframe load handler runs.

### whiteboard.js (V3.677, ink pipeline V3.683, mount API V3.684)
- **Purpose:** Live lecture whiteboard — named persistent boards drawn on a tablet, streamed to student browsers and a projector view in near-real-time. Generic: any class adds a `whiteboard` section via `SECTION_REG`.
- **Data:** `schedules/{classId}/whiteboards/{boardId}` board meta (`name`, `pages:[{id,background:blank|grid|ruled|axes}]`, `activePageId`, timestamps) + `strokes/{strokeId}` (`pageId`, `seq`, `color`, `w`, `pts:[x,y,pressure,...]` normalized to 16:10 board space, `done`). In-progress strokes flush every 300 ms as full-doc rewrites (RDP-simplified — see the ink pipeline below); docs chain past `MAX_PTS` local samples. `liveWhiteboard:{boardId,boardName,since}` merged onto the schedule doc drives the banner.
- **Roles:** drawing gated by `computeIsClassAdmin` (global admin / `ownerUid` / `classAdminEmails`), re-evaluated on `Auth.onChange`; viewers (incl. logged out) are read-only and auto-follow `activePageId` (manual flip pauses follow; chip re-engages). Firestore rules enforce the same gate server-side.
- **Input:** pointer events, pen+mouse ink only (iPad palm rejection), `getCoalescedEvents()`, pressure → per-segment line width; stroke eraser via polyline distance hit-test → doc delete; undo pops the session's own-stroke stack; clear-page is a two-tap confirm + chunked batch delete (no browser popups anywhere — inline forms + toasts).
- **Rendering:** two stacked canvases (background template + ink), devicePixelRatio-scaled, ResizeObserver refit, rAF-throttled repaint; live in-progress strokes paint incrementally (`activeLocalId` guards the pen-down stroke against snapshot echo clobber).
- **Ink resolution pipeline (V3.683)** — the seam to touch for any stroke-quality work, in three separable stages:
  1. *Capture* — `MIN_SEG` (0.0004) culls samples closer than ~0.5 px; positions `round5`, pressure `round2`.
  2. *Wire* — `simplifyToBudget` → `simplifyPts` (RDP, `SIMPLIFY_EPS`) runs on a **copy** at flush time (never the live array the pen is appending to), coarsening tolerance until the stored stroke fits `WIRE_MAX_PTS` (900). This is what makes denser capture cheaper than V3.677 rather than dearer — measured −20%…−82% bytes/stroke across pen-tremor levels 0–3 px. `MAX_PTS` (3000) bounds the *local* array and chains a new doc past it.
  3. *Render* — `paintStrokeRange` emits one cubic Bézier per segment from `crControls` (Catmull-Rom, curve passes through every sample). **End segments extrapolate a phantom neighbour** (`P0 = 3·P1 − 3·P2 + P3`, mirrored at the tail) rather than duplicating the endpoint — measured as the dominant error source (49% → 97.6%+ reduction vs straight chords), and it matters most for handwriting, where short strokes make end segments a large share of the total. `paintActiveSegment` repaints the last ~4 segments, since a segment's true shape depends on the sample *after* it; pen-up's full repaint clears the overdraw.
  - `LOW_LATENCY_CANVAS` (default **false**) gates the `desynchronized:true` context attribute — added speculatively in V3.678, reverted in V3.683 as a suspect for reduced ink fidelity. The first `getContext` call fixes context attributes for the canvas's life, so it is claimed in `sizeCanvases`.
- **Key exports:** `window.Whiteboard.renderSectionBody/attachLiveBanner/detachLiveBanner` (class-builder delegates); `McgheeLab.renderWhiteboardPage/wireWhiteboardPage` (app.js route `#/classes/{classId}/whiteboard/{boardId}`, `?projector=1` sets body class `wb-projector` hiding all chrome).

### teacher-classes.js (V3.304)
- **Purpose:** External teacher/student platform — everything outside teachers and their students touch on the main site. Teachers and students keep `role:'guest'` (RM stays sealed); all capabilities flow from `schedules.ownerUid` + `enrollments` membership, enforced by firestore.rules.
- **Lifecycle:** guest self-identifies as teacher (category flip) → submits `classRequests` doc → admin approves in RM (`rm/js/admin-teachers.js` batch: provision `schedules/{tc-…}` with `kind:'teacher-class'` + `grantedFolders` + `modules[]` expanded from `modules/manifest.json`, create `joinCodes/{CODE}`, flip requester category) → teacher shares the 6-char code → students enroll (`enrollments/{scheduleId}_{uid}`, create rules-gated on the live code doc) → both write reviews (pending → admin approves/features) → teacher submits a public profile (`teacherProfiles/{uid}`, admin-only `approved`).
- **Key exports (all on `window.McgheeLab`):**
  - `renderTeacherDashboard`/`wireTeacherDashboard` — request form + history, per-class block (folders, `enrollmentOpen` toggle, join-code copy/regenerate/disable, roster with remove), public-profile form (draft/submit, photo via shared crop/upload pipeline to `users/{uid}/teacher-photo`), review card
  - `renderStudentDashboard`/`wireStudentDashboard` — join-by-code, my classes, review card
  - `wireTeacherClassPage(scheduleId, schedule)` — student-facing class page states: signed-out → Google CTA; not enrolled → code entry; enrolled/owner/admin → numbered module list linking `#/classes/{id}/modules/{file}`
  - `joinClassWithCode(code)` — exact-id `get` on `joinCodes`, `enrollmentOpen` check, idempotent enrollment create/reactivate, then (V3.634) `TC_DB.linkStudentToTeacher` stamps `category:'student'` + `teacherUids: arrayUnion(teacherUid)` + `studentSchool`/`studentSince` on the joiner's user doc for every non-teacher. Those user-doc fields are owner-writable and therefore **denormalized display data, not a trust boundary** — `enrollments` (create rules-gated on a live code) stays authoritative for every access check. The RM Guests panel (`teachersOf`) reads all enrollment statuses and falls back to `teacherUids`, so "invited by …" survives removal and class deletion
  - `tcCanViewModules(classId, schedule)` — module-viewer soft gate (single enrollment `get`); consults the V3.636 teacher preview first
  - **View-as-student (V3.636)** — module-scope `_viewAs = {scheduleId, studentUid, studentName, status}` lets a teacher (or admin) render their own class page as one of their students: `viewAsStripHTML`/`wireViewAsStrip` draw the switcher in every gate state, `👁 View as` on each dashboard roster row is the other entry point, and `isOwner`/`isAdmin` are forced false while previewing. **Preview, not impersonation** — every read is one the teacher already owns (`rosterForTeacher`, a single `getEnrollment` whose `teacherUid` is the caller), the join form is short-circuited, and firestore.rules is unchanged. Scoped to one class page because a teacher cannot list a student's other enrollments — deliberately, so a student's other schools stay private. `_viewAs` carries its `scheduleId` (no leak across classes) and `canViewAsStudent` re-checks ownership every render (drops on sign-out)
  - `removeStudent(enrollmentId)` (V3.635) — teacher/admin removal stamps `removedBy:'teacher'` alongside `status:'removed'`. `removedBy` is outside the student-writable key set in the `/enrollments` update rule, so a removed student can no longer re-activate themselves with the code they already hold; a student may still leave and re-join with a live code, and the teacher clause can clear the stamp to re-admit them. `setEnrollmentStatus(id, status, joinCode)` writes the redeemed code on re-activation so the rule validates against a currently-live code (`request.resource.data` is the merged doc, so an untouched `joinCode` would otherwise still read live)
  - `renderClassReviewsSection(parentEl)` / `renderFeaturedTeachersSection(appEl)` — public sections called from app.js (#/classes strip, team-page teachers)
  - `TC_DB` — thin Firestore helpers for the five V3.304 collections
- **Auth timing:** `waitForAuth()` defers gate decisions until user-system's first `onAuthStateChanged` callback (`Auth._authStateResolved`), since class routes wire before auth resolves on cold loads.
- **Soft-gate caveat:** module HTML under `modules/` remains a public static asset; the gate is UI-level by design (accepted trade-off, see `CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.304_teacher_student_classes.md`).
- **Dependencies:** loaded after user-system.js + class-builder.js in index.html; uses `McgheeLab.{db, Auth, DB, openCropModal, processImage, uploadImageSet, renderGuestProfileCard, wireGuestProfileCard}`.
- **Demo seam (V3.632):** the module's data layer and acting identity are resolved through four one-line helpers — `demo()`, `src()`, `me()`, `myProfile()`. Every call site outside the `TC_DB` literal uses `src()`/`me()`, so `teacher-demo.js` can substitute an in-memory data layer and persona uid; with `McgheeLab.TC_DEMO` absent or inactive they return `TC_DB` and the signed-in uid (production path unchanged). `joinClassWithCode`'s three raw writes were folded into `TC_DB.createEnrollment`/`setUserCategory`/`getJoinCode` so the module has a single write surface for the seam to intercept.

**`users` collection read contract (V3.637)** — `users/{userId}` is no longer world-readable: `role != 'guest' || isOwner || isLabMember || isAdmin`. Because a Firestore `list` is denied outright when any doc it would return fails the rule, **any unauthenticated query of `users` must carry `where('role','!=','guest')`** — that is `McgheeLab.DB.getPublicProfiles()`, used by app.js's public team page. Signed-in lab members and admins keep the unconstrained `DB.getAllUsers()` (editor team pickers, admin user table). First-sign-in profile bootstrap reads `users/{uid}` before it exists; that still works because an errored operand (`resource.data` on a null resource) does not poison an `||` whose other side (`isOwner`) is true — asserted in `scripts/tests/teacher-rules.test.mjs`. Residual: lab-member documents remain publicly readable because the team page renders them straight from this collection; narrowing that requires mirroring public fields into `teamProfiles` first.

### teacher-demo.js (V3.632)
- **Purpose:** Admin-only preview of every external-user state. The V3.304 panels render only for `role:'guest'` users, so the admin account cannot reach them at all, and states like "request denied" or "removed student" need a multi-account round trip to manufacture. `#/demo` runs the real render/wire functions against in-memory fixtures.
- **Not a permissions test:** the browser stays signed in as the admin, so a read a real teacher would be denied still succeeds. Permission fidelity lives in `scripts/tests/teacher-rules.test.mjs` (62-check `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` suite over the V3.304 collections) and in the second-account pass documented in `CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.632_teacher_rules_findings.md`. The `#/demo` panel and the banner both state this.
- **Fixture world:** `baseWorld(manifest)` builds one shared cast (teacher Dana Ruiz, two classes, 15 students, three codes, three reviews, one public profile, one request); each of the 11 personas carries a `setup(world)` that trims the cast to its state, plus `uid`, `profile`, and the route it wants opened. Demo classes' `modules[]` are expanded from the real `modules/manifest.json` (stubbed synchronously, refreshed when the fetch resolves) so the class page and the module iframe load real module HTML.
- **`DEMO_DB`:** same ~23-method interface as `TC_DB`. Reads answer from the world; **writes mutate the world and append to an action log** instead of reaching Firestore, so join/regenerate/disable/remove/submit-review are genuinely exercised and the log shows what each would have written. The world is memory-only and resets on page reload; the persona id lives in `sessionStorage` so it survives in-tab navigation.
- **Host hooks (all inert when demo is off):** `app.js` — `#/demo` route (in `AUTH_GATED`) + `TC_DEMO.mountBanner(view)` after every render; `user-system.js` — demo dispatch at the top of `renderDashboard`/`wireDashboard` (before the `isGuest()` branch, since the previewing account is admin) and profile-card writes routed to `interceptProfileWrite`; `class-builder.js` — `resolveSchedule` and `wireModuleViewer` resolve `tc-demo-*` fixture classes before touching Firestore; `teacher-classes.js` — the `src()`/`me()` seam plus `demo().signedOut` for the signed-out gate.
- **Exports:** `McgheeLab.TC_DEMO` (`active`, `uid`, `profile`, `signedOut`, `db`, `log`, `start`, `stop`, `reset`, `schedule`, `note`, `interceptProfileWrite`, `mountBanner`, `renderPanel`, `wirePanel`), plus `McgheeLab.renderDemoPanel`/`wireDemoPanel` for the router.
- **Entry points:** `mcgheelab.com/#/demo`, and the `🎭 Demo mode` button in the RM Teachers toolbar (`rm/pages/admin-teachers.html`).

### lab-apps.js
- **Purpose (historical):** Lab Apps hub + iframe embedder — private section for authenticated lab members (non-guest)
- **Status (V3.53):** **No longer loaded.** V3.53 dropped the `<script defer src="lab-apps.js">` tag from [index.html](../../index.html). The file is preserved in the repo as **reference material for a future RM split-view feature** — the `_splitAppId` / `_splitRatio` harness inside this file (originally built to show two iframe-embedded lab apps side-by-side) is the pattern a future split-view in RM will adapt. Until that future work, the file's `LAB_APPS` registry, hub renderer, and iframe embedder are dead code that doesn't run anywhere. The `#/apps` SPA route in [app.js](../../app.js) is still technically registered but resolves to nothing useful — it'll be removed during a future workflow-driven SPA cleanup.
- **Key sections:**
  - **App registry (`LAB_APPS`):** Array of app definitions with `id`, `name`, `description`, `path` (to standalone `index.html`), `icon` (SVG), `status`, and `adminOnly` flag
  - **Hub renderer (`renderLabApps`):** Auth-gated grid of app cards; filters out `adminOnly` apps for non-admin users; redirects guests to dashboard and unauthenticated to login
  - **Iframe embedder (`renderLabApp(appId)`):** Renders `<iframe>` loading the app's standalone `index.html`; breadcrumb nav above; `wireLabApp` sends auth via postMessage
  - **Auth handshake (`wireLabApp`):** Listens for `mcgheelab-app-ready` from iframe → responds with `mcgheelab-auth` containing `user` and `profile` objects; also handles `mcgheelab-app-resize` for auto-sizing
- **Apps:** Inventory Tracker, Equipment Scheduler, Lab Meeting, Admin Console (admin-only), Activity Tracker, The Huddle, Scheduler
- **Routing:** `#/apps` (hub) and `#/apps/{appId}` (iframe embed) handled in `app.js` render/wire switches
- **Navigation:** ~~`#nav-apps` `<li>` shown when `Auth.currentUser` exists and `role !== 'guest'`~~ — **removed in V3.40.**
- **Exports:** `McgheeLab.renderLabApps`, `McgheeLab.wireLabApps`, `McgheeLab.renderLabApp`, `McgheeLab.wireLabApp`, `McgheeLab.LAB_APPS`

### apps/ (legacy — for reference only)
- **Purpose:** Self-contained mini-applications that run independently or embedded via iframe in the main site
- **Structure:** Each app has `index.html` (standalone entry point), `app.js` (logic), `styles.css` (app-specific styles)
- **Shared modules:**
  - `apps/shared/auth-bridge.js` — `McgheeLab.AppBridge` singleton; dual-mode auth: embedded (postMessage from parent) or standalone (Firebase `onAuthStateChanged`); exposes `init()`, `onReady(fn)`, `isEmbedded()`, `getUser()`, `getProfile()`, `isAdmin()`; standalone mode uses 2s grace period before treating null auth as sign-out (allows Firebase persistence to restore session from IndexedDB); embedded mode 8s timeout → auth wall fallback; recovery: if auth wall is showing and valid user arrives later, triggers `location.reload()` for clean restart; parent (`lab-apps.js`) also forwards auth to iframes via `Auth.onChange` listener for event-driven delivery
  - `apps/shared/app-base.css` — Dark theme variables (--bg, --surface, --accent, etc.), common components (.app-card, .app-btn, .app-input, .app-badge), auth wall, embedded/standalone body classes, responsive breakpoint at 600px; mobile shell styles (top bar, bottom bar, hamburger menu, filter dropdown, back button) active at ≤700px
  - `apps/shared/mobile-shell.js` — `McgheeLab.MobileShell` singleton; injects consistent phone navigation on all lab apps (except chat which handles its own); `configure({ appId, title })` to activate; creates sticky top bar (title + user avatar + hamburger), fixed bottom bar (5 app quick-nav icons + back arrow FAB); hamburger opens slide-in menu with all app links; auto-injects/removes on window resize; `setBackVisible(bool)` API for sub-page navigation
  - `apps/shared/calendar-service.js` — `McgheeLab.CalendarService` singleton; centralized multi-provider calendar integration (Google OAuth, Microsoft MSAL, Apple/ICS). Config persisted in `userSettings/{uid}.calendar`; OAuth tokens session-lived via shared `sessionStorage` keys. Exposes `init()`, `getEventsForDate()`, `connectGoogle()`, `disconnectGoogle()`, `connectOutlook()`, `disconnectOutlook()`, `importICSFile()`, `fetchAll()`, `onChange()`, `isConnected()`, `saveConfig()`, `dismissEvent()`, `restoreDismissed()`, `setEventStatus()`, `getEventStatus()`. ICS parsing, CORS proxy fallback chain (Firebase Cloud Function proxy first), configurable auto-refresh interval, per-event dismissal and busy-available status. Loaded by settings, activity tracker, huddle, and scheduler apps
  - `apps/shared/schedule-utils.js` — `McgheeLab.ScheduleUtils` singleton; pure time/week utility functions shared across huddle and scheduler: `getWeekDays()`, `fmtTime()`, `timeToSlot()`, `slotToTime()`, `timeLabels()`, `parseCalTimeToHHMM()`, `localDateStr()`, `todayStr()`, `getUserColor()`, `ZOOM_LEVELS`, `USER_COLORS`. No state or side effects
  - `apps/shared/schedule-service.js` — `McgheeLab.ScheduleService` singleton; schedule data layer managing Firestore subscriptions to `huddleScheduleTemplates` and `huddleScheduleOverrides`, plus `scheduleCustomEvents`. Exposes `init()`, `resolveScheduleForUser()` (template + override + custom event + calendar injection), `resolveAvailabilityOverlap()`, `saveScheduleTemplate()`, `addScheduleOverride()`, `deleteScheduleOverride()`, `saveCustomEvent()`, `deleteCustomEvent()`, `getLayerConfig()`, `saveLayerConfig()`, `setWeekOffset()`, `onChange()`. Constants: `UNAVAIL_REASONS`, `REASON_COLORS`, `MODE_COLORS`, `MODE_LABELS`. Loaded by scheduler and huddle apps
- **App list:**
  - ~~`apps/inventory/`~~ — **deleted in V3.43.** Was a 48-line stub; the real inventory management system is at [rm/pages/inventory.html](../../rm/pages/inventory.html) (8 tabs, 30+ subcategories, multi-location stock, LIVE_SYNC).
  - `apps/equipment/` — Equipment Scheduler: full booking system for shared lab instruments. Tab layout (Calendar, My Bookings, Admin). Weekly CSS Grid calendar (7am-9pm, 30-min slots, 7 days) and monthly dot-grid view with per-device filtering dropdown. Priority color coding (normal/high/urgent/maintenance) with customizable colors. Booking modal with conflict detection, duration constraints, and advance-day limits. Training/permission system: admin defines certification types, assigns per user, devices require specific certs; co-operator requirement forces lower-category users (undergrads) to select a grad+ co-operator. Admin panels: device CRUD, training checkbox table, settings. Google Calendar push-sync via Google Identity Services OAuth (admin-driven, per-device calendar IDs). Real-time via Firestore `onSnapshot`. Data: `equipment/{equipmentId}` (catalog), `equipmentBookings/{bookingId}` (reservations), `equipmentTraining/{uid}` (certs), `equipmentSettings/config` (singleton)
  - `apps/meetings/` — Lab Meeting: weekly meeting management with fixed-rotation presentation scheduling, collaborative agenda builder (any member adds items), shared notes, action item tracking with cross-meeting carry-over, and post-presentation cross-pollination signals (reaction chips: interesting/questions/collaborate/relevant). Sidebar+main layout with 5 sections: Next Meeting, Schedule, Archive, My Items, Settings. Admin generates semester meetings from config (day/time/skip dates/rotation order). Data: `meetings/{meetingId}` (embedded agendaItems[], actionItems[], feedback[] arrays), `meetingConfig/settings` (rotation, semester config). Real-time via Firestore `onSnapshot`
  - ~~`apps/console/`~~ — **deleted in V3.42.** Was a 65-line stub; the four promised admin functions (app management, user permissions, integrations, usage logs) live elsewhere in RM (nav gating in [rm/js/nav.js](../../rm/js/nav.js), future `rm/pages/admin.html`, [rm/pages/settings.html](../../rm/pages/settings.html), [rm/pages/api-usage.html](../../rm/pages/api-usage.html)).
  - `apps/activity-tracker/` — Activity Tracker: daily activity logging with hierarchical categories, ML categorization (Naive Bayes), AI categorization (Anthropic API), milestone tracking, voice input, Chart.js analytics dashboard. Privacy: strictly owner-only Firestore rules. Data: `trackerData/{userId}` (settings, categories, ML model) + `trackerEntries/{userId}/entries/{entryId}` subcollection (task entries with date, categoryPath, duration, milestone, source)
  - `apps/huddle/` — The Huddle: community-driven weekly planning board. Lab members post planned protocols/tasks for the week, others sign up to watch or join. Real-time feed via Firestore `onSnapshot`, week navigation, check-in prompts, protocol linking, status management (completed/cancelled/delayed/skipped). **The Rundown:** non-timeframe task list per week with admin-configurable categories and project associations; join-request workflow where others request to shadow/help, owner accepts and schedules onto the huddle calendar with availability overlap detection. **Lab Schedule:** recurring weekly availability template with per-week overrides; blocks typed as available/unavailable with reasons and rigid/flexible rigidity; Team Availability Gantt view shows all members' schedules per day. Data: `huddlePlans`, `huddleCheckins`, `huddleProtocols`, `huddleRundown` (weekly tasks with joinRequests array), `huddleConfig/settings` (admin-managed categories), `huddleScheduleTemplates/{userId}` (recurring weekly blocks), `huddleScheduleOverrides` (per-week deviations)
  - `apps/scheduler/` — Scheduler: standalone scheduling app moved from dashboard. List view with create/manage/delete; editor view using `McgheeLab.Scheduler` engine with admin/guest/public view switching, guest management, session builder, freeform availability. Self-contained ScheduleDB for Firestore CRUD. Loads `scheduler.js` via script tag. Data: reuses existing `schedules` and `participants` Firestore collections
  - `apps/chat/` — Lab Chat: real-time messaging with channels, DMs, threads, reactions, @mentions, read receipts, and Google Drive file sharing. Desktop: three-panel layout (sidebar + message feed + optional thread panel). Mobile (≤700px): conversation-list-first design with view state machine (`_mobileView`: list/conversation/files); conversation list shows all subscribed channels + DMs with preview/badges; filter dropdown (newest/active/unread/alpha); conversation view replaces sidebar with stats bar (readers/search/files); files view groups channel attachments by type; bottom bar with 5 app quick-nav icons + back arrow FAB; hamburger menu for browse/DM/contacts/search/settings. Subscription-based notifications: all channels visible, users subscribe for alerts. Admin-defined channel categories with channel directory browser. User-organized sidebar with draggable custom groups. Google Drive integration via Google Identity Services OAuth for file uploads to shared lab folder. Browser notifications for @mentions and DMs. Data: `chatConfig/settings` (categories, Drive config), `chatChannels/{channelId}` (metadata + denormalized lastMessage), `chatMessages/{messageId}` (messages with reactions map, readBy array, thread fields), `chatReadState/{uid_channelId}` (per-user read tracking), `chatUserMeta/{uid}` (subscriptions, sidebar layout, prefs)
- **Execution modes:** Embedded (`.app-embedded` class, header hidden, auth via postMessage) vs Standalone (`.app-standalone` class, header visible, auth via Firebase direct)
- **Script load order in standalone:** Firebase SDK (compat) → `../../firebase-config.js` → `../shared/auth-bridge.js` → `../shared/mobile-shell.js` → `../shared/calendar-service.js` → `app.js` (chat app omits mobile-shell.js and calendar-service.js)
- **Status (V3.40):** All 12 apps are reachable through the new RM nav via iframe-bridge wrappers in [rm/pages/app-*.html](../../rm/pages/) — see *rm/* below. The standalone `/apps/<name>/` URLs still work as a fallback during the multi-version migration. Phase B (V3.41–V3.52) replaces each iframe wrapper with a native RM page; Phase C (V3.53) deletes `/apps/` entirely.

### rm/ (ResearchManagement)
- **Purpose:** Auth-gated lab dashboard at `mcgheelab.com/rm/`. As of V3.40 this is the consolidating home for every lab tool — the 12 lab apps (currently iframe-bridged) plus the migrated public-site dashboard/admin/cv/guide editors (in progress, V3.43–V3.45).
- **Source of truth:** This `/rm/` tree is the canonical RM source — edit here directly, not the sibling `ResearchManagement/` repo. Detailed RM-internal architecture lives in [rm/CLAUDE.md](../../rm/CLAUDE.md).
- **Data layer:** Every Firestore path is registered in [rm/js/api-routes.js](../../rm/js/api-routes.js); call sites use `api.load(path)` / `api.save(path, data)` from [rm/js/util.js](../../rm/js/util.js). (V3.647: util.js also exports `rerenderPreservingScroll(el, renderFn)` / `scrollParentOf(el)` — scroll-anchored re-render for any panel sharing a scroll container with other independently-repainting panels. NOTE `api` is a top-level `const`: it is a lexical global and `window.api` is ALWAYS undefined — guard with `typeof api !== 'undefined'`, never `window.api`.) The adapter at [rm/js/api-firestore-adapter.js](../../rm/js/api-firestore-adapter.js) routes to either `userData/{uid}/<subcollection>` (per-user, `scope: 'user'`) or a top-level lab collection (`scope: 'lab'`, admin-write). IndexedDB cache via [rm/js/local-cache.js](../../rm/js/local-cache.js) with smart `MAX(updatedAt)` revalidation.
- **Auth gate:** [rm/js/firebase-bridge.js](../../rm/js/firebase-bridge.js) — `firebridge.requireSignIn('reason')` (V3.338, the default gated entry: signed-out visitors get an inline sign-in card — shared `_signInFormHtml`/`_wireSignInForm` component with the nav dropdown — page DOM is stashed in `#fb-gate-stash` and restored after sign-in so boot continues without reload; a sign-out watcher re-gates mid-session) / `firebridge.gateAdmin('reason')` (builds on requireSignIn) / `firebridge.whenAuthResolved()` (infrastructure consumers only — resolves degraded `{degraded:true}` after 10s if the profile never loads; `_loadProfile` retries 3× with backoff). `firebridge.retryProfile()` + `PROFILE_BOOTSTRAP.retry()` recover a failed profile load from the nav chip. `firebridge.notifyAccessIssue(context)` renders the `#fb-access-banner` on mid-session permission-denied (wired into the adapter's load/subscribe and `firebridge.onSnapshot`; adapter returns typed-empty instead of legacy-JSON fallback on denial while signed in). Anyone can sign in via Google but profile-bootstrap creates `users/{uid}` as `role: 'guest'`; `firestore.rules` `isLabMember()` requires `role != 'guest'`; firebridge renders a full-page pending-access overlay until admin promotes them. The `#dnav-rm` link in the public-site nav appears only after sign-in (regardless of role).
- **Live sync:** [rm/js/live-sync-helper.js](../../rm/js/live-sync-helper.js) — `LIVE_SYNC.attach({paths, refresh, tag})` debounces remote updates, suppresses post-save blink, deduplicates subscriptions across pages.
- **Top nav (V3.40 layout):** Six groups in [rm/js/nav.js](../../rm/js/nav.js): **Dashboard** | **Activity** (Tracker, Overview, Calendar, Email, Tasks, Sharing, Year) | **Research** (Projects, Library, Comments, Papers, Teaching, Service) | **Operations** _gate: lab-member_ (Chat, Huddle, Meetings, Scheduler, Equipment) | **Lab Admin** _gate: lab-member_ (Compliance, Chemical Safety, Inventory, Lab Members, Important People, Career & Tenure, Procurement, Purchase Requests, Grant Accounts, Budget, Analytics, Travel) | **Settings** _gate: lab-member_ (Profile, Settings, CV Overview, CV Editor, Member Activity _gate: admin_).
- **Iframe-bridge tier (RETIRED — V3.53):** Phase A introduced 5 iframe-bridge wrappers under [rm/pages/app-*.html](../../rm/pages/) that loaded `/apps/<name>/` in an iframe and forwarded auth via postMessage. Phase B (V3.41–V3.52) progressively replaced each wrapper's contents with a `<meta refresh>` redirect to its native port. V3.53 deleted all five files outright. Bookmarks pinned to those URLs return 404 after V3.53.
- **Native ports (Phase B, in progress):**
  - **V3.536–V3.541 — Weekly Focus program (My Week II, complete):** the mentor↔mentee focus loop on top of My Week. Hierarchy is explicit — a FOCUS (the week's why) contains `tasks[]` (the concrete what), deliberately separate from the buckets system. Core engine [rm/js/day-distribute.js](../../rm/js/day-distribute.js) (`window.DAY_DISTRIBUTE`) treats a My Week item (`userData/{uid}/dayPlans/{itemId}`) as the hub record and fans it out via per-surface adapters (huddle, equipment, notebook, tracker, task, pmr_week), each using a **deterministic destination doc id** (`day-<itemId>` / `auto-dayplan-<itemId>`) for idempotent create/update/retry. Cascade: item saves first, fan-out is `Promise.allSettled` (failures → per-surface retry chips), delete cascades cancel/remove every copy — EXCEPT notebook entries with user content, which **orphan** (kept, noted) rather than deleted; the notebook is canonical for "what I did" per this program. Persistent prefs doc `dayPlans/_prefs` (`auto_distribute` ON by default + per-surface exclusions). Only rules change: `equipmentBookings` create/owner-edit whitelists gain an optional `source_ref` map (additive; deploy rules before FTP).
