  - **V3.109 — Paper builder: equation library + right-click insert + numbered references:** Closes the wishlist quartet. New paper-level `paperMap.equation_library: Y.Array<Y.Map>` (each entry `{id, name (Y.Text), latex (Y.Text)}`) holds reusable inline equations. New [rm/js/paper-equations.js](../../rm/js/paper-equations.js) mounts an Equations slide-out panel anchored to the right edge from a `📐 Equations` topbar button (mirrors the V3.104 claim-detail panel pattern). Two panel sections: Inline library (full CRUD + KaTeX preview per entry) and Numbered equations (read-only doc-order list of `attrs.numbered && attrs.display` blocks with their assigned 1-based number; click → scroll editor + flash). Right-click `contextmenu` on any paragraph body fires a custom menu with `Insert inline equation` (picker over library) + `Insert equation reference` (picker over numbered equations); both pickers float at the click point, type-to-filter, render KaTeX previews per row, ↑/↓/Enter/Esc keybinds. Click → restore caret + `document.execCommand('insertText', …)` of the relevant token. Two new paragraph tokens land in [rm/js/paper-editor.js](../../rm/js/paper-editor.js)'s `renderParagraphHtml` scanner: `[!eqi:<id>]` → `renderInlineEqLibraryChip(id)` (KaTeX inline of the library entry; faded `[?eq]` for unknown ids) and `[!eqr:<label>]` → `renderEqRefChip(label)` (`Eq. <n>` chip whose number tracks the doc-order numbering walker). Doc-order numbering walker `getNumberedEquations()` traverses sections → children, returns `[{blockId, label, num, latex}]`. `bindYTextToContentEditable` listens for the `paper-equations-changed` window event and re-renders rendered HTML when the source contains either token, so chips stay in sync without requiring a focus blur. [rm/js/paper-blocks.js](../../rm/js/paper-blocks.js)'s `renderEquation` toolbar gains a Numbered checkbox (auto-flips display=true), a label input (auto-prefixes `eq:`, slugifies, capped at MAX_EQ_LABEL_LENGTH=64), and a `pe-eq-num-badge` that subscribes to `paper-equations-changed`. [rm/js/paper-export-tex.js](../../rm/js/paper-export-tex.js)'s `paragraphTextToTex` resolves `[!eqi:<id>]` → `\(<latex>\)` against a `_exportEqLibrary` set/cleared around section rendering by `runExport`; `[!eqr:<label>]` → `\eqref{<label>}`. `equationToTex` now distinguishes three cases: numbered+display → `\begin{equation}\label{<label>}…\end{equation}`, unnumbered display → `\[…\]`, inline → `\(…\)`. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.109_equation_library.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.109_equation_library.md). **No schema migration**; existing equation blocks unchanged until the user opts in to numbering.
  - **V3.107 — Paper builder: body rich text:** Paragraph bodies gain inline-markdown emphasis. [rm/js/paper-editor.js](../../rm/js/paper-editor.js)'s `renderParagraphHtml` scanner extends to five new tokens — `**bold**` → `<strong>`, `*italic*` → `<em>`, `~sub~` → `<sub>`, `^sup^` → `<sup>`, `` `code` `` → `<code>` — each with a strict accept rule (no boundary whitespace, no newlines, no embedded same-delimiter for single-char tokens). Bold tested before italic so `**foo**` matches as bold rather than as two adjacent italics. All tokens except code spans recurse through the same scanner, so `**Smith [@smith2024] showed $x^2$**` resolves cleanly with nested cite chip + KaTeX inside the bold. Two new utilities exposed on `window.PaperEditor`: `wrapSelectionInTokens(lhs, rhs)` (routes through `document.execCommand('insertText', …)` so the existing Y.Text binding picks up the diff via its input listener; falls back to Range-API `deleteContents`/`insertNode`+`dispatchEvent('input')` when execCommand isn't supported; moves caret back by `rhs.length` when there was no original selection so user can type inside the empty pair) and `richTextKeydownHandler(e)` (maps Cmd/Ctrl+B/I/E to the corresponding wrap; declines when Shift/Alt are held to leave room for native browser shortcuts). [rm/js/paper-blocks.js](../../rm/js/paper-blocks.js)'s `renderParagraph` wraps the body contenteditable in a flex column (`<div.pe-paragraph-body-wrap>`) with a 5-button toolbar (B / I / X₂ / X² / `<>`) above; buttons use mousedown.preventDefault to keep caret in body. View-mode toggle (`applyMode`) hides/shows the wrap (toolbar + body together) so skeleton-only view hides the toolbar too. Toolbar gated on `ctx.editable`. [rm/js/paper-export-tex.js](../../rm/js/paper-export-tex.js)'s `paragraphTextToTex` rewritten to route the same five tokens to `\textbf{}` / `\emph{}` / `\textsubscript{}` / `\textsuperscript{}` / `\texttt{}`; code spans are protected first via a null-byte sentinel placeholder so their content can't be corrupted by later markdown passes. **No schema migration** — Y.Text wire format unchanged. Skeleton bullets, equation source, and figure layout inputs deliberately don't get the toolbar (skeleton is argument scaffolding, equation is LaTeX source, figure layout is structured fields). Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.107_body_rich_text.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.107_body_rich_text.md). Wishlist item 4 (equation refs + numbering) follows in V3.108+.

Each Y.Map is `{id, depth, text: Y.Text, claim_id}` so two coauthors editing different bullets never collide at the character level. New `migrateSkeletonToItems(yBlock, Y)` runs once per block at first render post-deploy: splits the legacy flat text on `\n`, parses leading spaces ÷ 2 → depth (capped at `MAX_SKELETON_DEPTH = 3`), strips leading `- ` prefix, idempotent. [rm/pages/paper-builder.html](../../rm/pages/paper-builder.html) loads `claims.js` + `paper-bullet-claims.js` before `paper-blocks.js`. [rm/js/paper-editor.js](../../rm/js/paper-editor.js) calls `PaperBulletClaims.attach(state.paperId)` right after the Yjs connect resolves. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.104_skeleton_claims.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.104_skeleton_claims.md). Wishlist items 3 (body rich text) and 4 (equation refs) follow in V3.105+.
  - **V3.102 — Paper builder: editable figure block:** [rm/js/paper-blocks.js](../../rm/js/paper-blocks.js)'s `renderFigure(yBlock, ctx)` replaces the long-standing `renderUnsupported('Figure')` dispatch. Each figure block has `body: Y.Text` (caption, bound via the existing `bindYTextToContentEditable` so `[@cite]` and `$math$` tokens render the same way they do in paragraphs) plus an `attrs: Y.Map` carrying `storage_path` / `download_url` / `hash` / `mime` (Storage pointer + dedup metadata) and `width` / `placement` / `centering` / `label` / `alt` (LaTeX `\includegraphics` options). New helper [rm/js/paper-figures.js](../../rm/js/paper-figures.js) wraps Firebase Cloud Storage uploads at `paper-figures/{paperId}/{shortHash}.{ext}` with the same SHA-256 dedup pattern as [rm/js/library-upload.js](../../rm/js/library-upload.js); allowlist is PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP/SVG + PDF, 15 MB cap, content-type guard mirrored in [storage.rules](../../storage.rules) under a fresh `paper-figures/{paperId}/{=**}` matcher (kept distinct from the PDF-only `papers/{paperId}/` matcher so neither rule loosens the other). [rm/js/paper-editor.js](../../rm/js/paper-editor.js)'s `addFigure(secId)` mirrors `addEquation` and is gated by `PaperSchemas.styleFor(section).allowFigures`; render-block ctx now carries `paperId`. [rm/js/paper-export-tex.js](../../rm/js/paper-export-tex.js)'s `figureToTex` reads the new attrs first (falls back to legacy `attrs.path` / `attrs.raw_tex`), routes the caption through `paragraphTextToTex`, and emits `\begin{figure}[<placement>]\centering\includegraphics[width=<width>]{figures/<basename>}\caption{...}\label{<label>}\end{figure}` — the export server is expected to mirror the Storage blob into `<repo>/figures/`. [rm/pages/paper-builder.html](../../rm/pages/paper-builder.html) loads `firebase-storage-compat.js` and `paper-figures.js` in editor mode. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.102_figures.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.102_figures.md). Companion writer-side wishlist items (skeleton outlining + claims, body rich text, equation refs) follow in V3.103-V3.105.
  - **V3.86 — Library paper reader: citations + overlays + .md import + search:** [rm/pages/library-paper.html](../../rm/pages/library-paper.html) gains four lit-review modules that compose with the existing PDF.js viewer + annotation system rather than rewriting it. **[rm/js/paper-citations.js](../../rm/js/paper-citations.js)** parses references from the back of the paper on `_viewer.ready()` and lists inline-citation tokens for the visible page in the left sidebar with bidirectional hover-to-flash and a "+ Add to library" stub-create per cited DOI. **[rm/js/paper-overlays.js](../../rm/js/paper-overlays.js)** adds a project-bucket scope key (`bucket_ids[]`) to annotations: a popover toggles which buckets render, multiple stack with deterministic-color left-edge stripes, new highlights are stamped with the active set. Bucket linking reuses [rm/js/links.js](../../rm/js/links.js); active-state lives in `localStorage.rm_lp_overlays_<paperId>`. **[rm/js/paper-overlay-import.js](../../rm/js/paper-overlay-import.js)** handles drag-drop of `.paper-overlay.md` files (frontmatter `paper_id`/`bucket_id` + `## Highlight` blocks); the parser validates each `quote` against the page text layer (fuzzy whitespace), shows a per-highlight match preview modal, and idempotently writes matched ones via `ANNOTATION_SYNC.create`. Companion authoring aid at **[.claude/skills/paper-overlay/SKILL.md](../../.claude/skills/paper-overlay/SKILL.md)** for sibling VSCode lit-review repos. **[rm/js/paper-search.js](../../rm/js/paper-search.js)** adds keyword search across the paper with hits inside existing highlights ranked first; click a result jumps + flashes the rect. [rm/js/library-paper.js](../../rm/js/library-paper.js) initializes each module after `_mountViewer`, composes `PAPER_OVERLAYS.getFilterFn` AND with `ANNOTATION_PANEL.getFilterFn`, and stamps `bucket_ids` on `ANNOTATION_OVERLAY.onCreate`. [rm/js/annotation-overlay.js](../../rm/js/annotation-overlay.js) draws the per-bucket stripes; [rm/js/annotation-panel.js](../../rm/js/annotation-panel.js) gains optional `getBuckets`/`getBucketColor`/`onBucketToggle` opts and an "Overlays" chip row in the info panel. [rm/js/annotation-sync.js](../../rm/js/annotation-sync.js) carries `bucket_ids: []` in defaults; no firestore.rules edit needed (annotation rule allows owner writes of arbitrary fields). [rm/js/library-upload.js](../../rm/js/library-upload.js) exports a new `fromDoi(doi)` for the Add-to-library button.
- **Production deploy:** Cyberduck FTP the McGheeLabWebsite repo to godaddy — the `/rm/` subdir lands at `mcgheelab.com/rm/`. No build step. Firebase rules / indexes / Cloud Functions deploy from the McGheeLabWebsite repo root via `firebase deploy --only ...`.

### modules/ (learning module pages)
- **Purpose:** Standalone full-page HTML lesson files with auto-navigating class-specific headers. Each module is a self-contained page that loads outside the SPA.
- **Structure:** `modules/{folder}/` directories contain lesson HTML files (folders are by topic/course — e.g. `tfm/`, `bme576/`, `foundations/` — not strictly a classId); `modules/shared/` contains the header component; `modules/_template.html` is the starter template; `modules/manifest.json` catalogs all module files grouped by folder (`folders.{folder}.label` + `files[]` of `{name, title}`) and is read by the class-builder admin UI's module picker
- **Equipment Foundations, lesson 04 (V3.720):** `modules/equipment/04-the-plasma-cleaner.html` — Harrick
  PDC-001-HP + PlasmaFlo, 10 sims. Instrument-first against `surface_functionalization/02`, which owns the
  surface chemistry. First lesson in the track sourced from a vendor **website** rather than a PDF manual;
  the retrieved datasheets and the PDC32G-M-03 manual now live in `Data/equipment/`. Lessons 05–08 renumbered.
- **Equipment Foundations (V3.690):** `modules/equipment/` — `overview.html` + three of seven lessons
  (`01-the-balance`, `02-the-pipette`, `03-labware-and-consumables`), 27 sims and 32 numbered equations.
  Same framework layer as cell_culture, and the same no-rail decision. Instrument-first, where
  cell_culture is technique-first; the two overlap on hardware deliberately. Five tabs mapped to Alex's
  five sections, so the **capstone is tab 5** here rather than tab 4. Built from the vendor manuals in
  `Data/equipment/`, with every quoted tolerance carrying its document number.
- **Section engine (V3.692, extended V3.693):** `modules/cell_culture/01-the-cabinet.html` renders one
  cabinet cross-section for five sections (§2.1, §3.1–§3.4) via `cabAir()` + `secGeom`/
  `secBox`/`secPath`/`secTracers`/`planGeom`, parameterised by an `env` describing what
  each section puts in the cabinet. Any further section that needs the cabinet drawn
  should call the engine rather than draw its own.
- **Framework note (V3.691):** the shared widget layer's `RESET` hook fires on *every*
  slider `input`, which silently restarts any animated field. Lesson 1 now guards its
  continuous fields with `keepField()` behind a `RESEED` flag raised only at boot and in
  `setScen()`. Copy that guard into any new module that pairs `registerAnim` with `reset`.
- **Cell Culture Foundations (V3.686, Lesson 1 rebuilt through V3.694):** `modules/cell_culture/` —
  `overview.html` + four lessons (`01-the-cabinet`, `02-the-incubator`, `03-the-hands`,
  `04-aliquoting-and-stewardship`). Lesson 1 now runs **6 tabs / 13 widgets / 13 equations**, with
  five of its sections drawn by the shared cabinet-section engine. Built to the BME466 spec's 5-tab arc (Fundamentals → Phenomenon → Synthesis →
  `cap-tab` → `next-tab`) on the AUTHORING.md §9 framework layer — `defWidget`/`registerAnim`, one shared
  rAF loop, geometric `syncVis()` — but **without the §9 section rail and Present mode**, which Alex
  declined. `TABW` and the initial `activeTab` are read from the DOM, so that framework block is byte-identical
  across all four lessons. One framework change came out of it: **`statTick` now bypasses rate-limiting for
  widgets with no `registerAnim`** — a static widget draws once per input, so an input landing inside the
  ~6 Hz window used to leave its readouts stale permanently. Because the track has no `#rail`, the V3.684
  module whiteboard panel (which mounts into `.rail-head`) does not apply to it, and `class-builder.js`
  keeps scrollHeight-sizing its iframes.
- **Cell Culture Lesson 1 rebuild (V3.687):** `01-the-cabinet.html` diverges from the
  other three lessons in three ways worth knowing before editing it. (a) It renders **paired
  canvases** — `cv-{key}` plus a second view `cv-{key}-side` / `cv-{key}-top` — inside
  `.chart-row`; only the primary carries `st-`/`vd-`. (b) Its `solved` tab holds **two
  pointer-driven widgets**, `layout` (a drag-and-drop builder plus an animated run) and
  `check` (a three-stage graded concept check whose last stage is dragged by hand); both are
  wired by `wireLayout()` / `wireCheck()` at boot, next to `wireAll()`. (c) The §4 model is
  the one place in the track where **the physics is about the operator**, not the cabinet:
  the sleeve runs from the hand back out through the opening (`armTail`), the shoulder tracks
  the hand (`shoulderX`), and the task list is a **waypoint** list so leg N+1 starts where leg
  N ended — writing it as independent (from, to) pairs let the automatic run teleport and
  score a layout clean that the same layout failed under a real drag.
- **Cell Culture Lesson 2 (V3.688):** `02-the-incubator.html` is the track's only
  **six-tab** lesson, and the only file where the equation-number tab index does not
  match the tab position — both deliberate, both explained in the version entry above
  and in the file's own equation index. Its §1.2 `stack` widget renders **two maps over
  one geometry** (fill = temperature, border = sleeve traffic) which is the pattern to
  copy whenever two correct rules disagree; §4.1 reuses Lesson 1's eq. 1.3.2 for a door
  instead of a hand, which is the intended way to reuse across lessons.
- **Cell Culture Lesson 1 airflow (V3.689):** the numbers in §2.1 are not free
  parameters — cabinet width, filter-face area, the sash tolerance and the volume
  ledger all come from the 1300 Series A2 operating manual in `Data/equipment/`, and
  changing one without re-reading it will break the arithmetic the worked example asks
  the student to check. The compensating `vIn()` (velocity held, volume varied) is
  specific to a SmartFlow-class cabinet; the `old` scenario chip preserves the
  fixed-blower model for everything else.
- **Lab Foundations overview (V3.287):** `modules/foundations/overview.html` — beginner-facing landing for a series of topic tracks (Hydrogel Mechanics live + scaffolded "coming soon" tracks). Attached as the first lesson of a Firestore class. Its inline script makes track links class-aware: derives `classId` from `?class=` or, inside the SPA iframe, the parent hash; opens in-iframe links in a new tab with `?class=` (top-nav is sandboxed off) so the target module renders its own prev/next, else navigates in place / falls back to bare `../{folder}/<file>`
- **Solid Mechanics Foundations (V3.296):** `modules/solid_mechanics/` — a five-lesson standalone course (`01-atoms-as-springs` → `02-grains-and-boundaries` → `03-honey-cheese-metal-diamond` → `04-stress-and-strain` → `05-loading-modes`) authored per `modules/AUTHORING.md`. Fully self-contained: MathJax CDN only, **no** `module-header.js`/Firebase includes; opens directly or over FTP. Each file carries an identical inline `<style>` block and a shared JS helper library (`setupCanvas`, `Chart`, `drawLine/arrow/springGlyph/dashpotGlyph`, `fmt/niceTicks`, `setStat/setVerdict`, seeded RNG) above a per-module `PER-MODULE` divider; every tab drives a live canvas sim through a `DRAW` dispatch map guarded by try/catch. `setupCanvas` caches each canvas's intrinsic logical size in `dataset` (not re-read from the DPR-reflected `width` attribute) so redraws are stable on Retina. Registered in `manifest.json` under the `solid_mechanics` folder (label "Solid Mechanics Foundations"). The folder also ships `overview.html` — a course landing page on the `foundations/overview.html` infrastructure (dark-theme hero, shared `module-header` + Firebase includes, class-aware `?class=` link propagation, new-tab links inside the SPA iframe) pairing each lesson with its worksheet — and five printable `worksheet-0N-*.html` companions (predict→experiment→record→explain, dependency-free, print CSS).
- **Shared modules:**
  - `modules/shared/module-header.js` — `McgheeLab.ModuleHeader` singleton; reads `?class={scheduleId}` and (V3.716) `?mod={placementId}` URL params; fetches `schedules/{classId}` from Firestore; `getModuleRef()` + an id-first resolve (`find(m => m.id === modRef) || find(m => m.htmlFile === currentFile)`) locates the current placement; prev/next and "Lesson N of M" walk that placement's `sectionId`; `moduleLink(mod, classId)` carries `&mod=` onto sibling links; builds header with back link, progress indicator, title, prev/next nav, homework button; graceful degradation on error
  - `modules/shared/module-header.css` — Sticky header bar with dark theme variables matching `app-base.css`; three-zone layout (back link | center title + progress | nav buttons); responsive stacking at 600px
- **Script load order:** Firebase SDK (app + firestore compat only) → `../../firebase-config.js` → `../shared/module-header.js`
- **Data model:** Modules registered as `modules[]` array on `schedules/{classId}` Firestore doc: `{ id, sectionId, title, htmlFile, folder, order, homeworkFileId, published, kind? }`
  - **`sectionId` (V3.716)** — the `tabs[].sections[].id` of the "Learning Modules" section this entry belongs to. The array stays flat and class-wide; it is **partitioned** by this field, which is what makes each modules section its own instance. Entries with no `sectionId` (pre-V3.716) or a stale one are adopted by the **first** modules section, so a deleted section re-homes its lessons rather than orphaning them. Teacher-classes have `tabs: []` and therefore never carry a `sectionId` — the normalizer bails and their navigation stays class-wide.
  - **`id` has two conventions.** Class-builder mints `mod_`/`notes_` + 8 random hex per placement (`class-builder.js`, `generateKey()`); the teacher catalog mints the deterministic `{folder}--{basename}` (`rm/js/admin-teachers.js` `catalogModuleId`, matching the `teacherCatalog/{id}` doc id). Both are unique within a class, which is all the router requires.
- **Navigation:** Links from the class page carry `?class=`; the iframe src also carries `&mod={placementId}` (V3.716) so the module's own header can scope prev/next. Prev/next links are sibling files in the same directory with both params preserved.
  - **Student state is keyed on the LESSON, not the placement** — deliberate, decided with Alex in V3.716. The notes/homework boards (`schedules/{classId}/{notesBoards|hwBoards}/{moduleKey}_{uid}`, where `moduleKey` is `<meta name="ml-module-key">` or the filename basename) and `hwProgress/{assignment}_{uid}` are unchanged. Filing one lesson under two sections must not split or hide a student's work, and re-keying would have orphaned every existing board and progress doc. `&mod=` is for navigation only; nothing keys storage on it.

### functions/ (Firebase Cloud Functions)
- **Purpose:** Server-side push notification pipeline — Firestore-triggered Cloud Functions that send FCM messages to lab members when events occur
- **Runtime:** Node.js 20, Firebase Cloud Functions v2 (2nd gen)
- **Entry point:** `functions/index.js` — initializes Firebase Admin SDK, exports 6 Cloud Functions
- **Helpers:**
  - `functions/helpers/notify.js` — `sendToUsers(db, messaging, userIds, notif, appKey)`: checks `userSettings/{uid}` for master + per-app notification toggles, fetches tokens from `users/{uid}/pushTokens`, sends via `messaging.sendEach()`, auto-deletes stale tokens on send failure
  - `functions/helpers/users.js` — `sendToAllMembers(db, messaging, notif, appKey, excludeUids)`: queries all `users` docs, filters excludes, delegates to `sendToUsers`
- **Functions:**
  - `chat.js` → `onChatMessageCreate`: Firestore trigger on `chatMessages` create; reads channel info, queries `chatUserMeta` for subscribers; respects muted channels and mentionsOnly prefs; routes DMs via `dmChannelIds`
  - `voice-call.js` → `onVoiceCallCreate`: Firestore trigger on `voiceCalls/{channelId}` create (V3.525) — FCM "ring" to the chat channel's recipients (`members[]` DM / `subscriberUids[]` channel) minus the starter, muted channels respected; deep link `chat.html?channel=<id>`
  - `huddle.js` → `onHuddlePlanUpdate`: detects new joiners/watchers (notifies owner) and status changes (notifies participants); `onHelpRequestCreate`: broadcasts to all members; `onHelpRequestUpdate`: notifies owner on new response
  - `equipment.js` → `onEquipmentBookingCreate`: notifies equipment managers on pending-approval bookings; `onEquipmentBookingUpdate`: notifies booker on confirmed/displaced status changes
  - `task-market.js` (V3.314) → `onMarketPostCreated`: directed `taskMarket` post → pushes the target (handoff ask when `open`, plain task-sent when admin pre-`accepted`); `kind:'request'` → pushes all admins; undirected offers silent. `onMarketPostUpdated`: fires only on the `open → claimed/accepted/declined` edge → pushes the post creator. appKey `tasks`. Companion guard: `tasks.js`'s `onTaskAssigned` skips tasks carrying `marketPostId` (market-materialized copies would double-push).
  - `release-announce.js` → `releaseAnnounce` (HTTPS, V3.604): admin-only "What's New" broadcast — POST `{version, title?, summary?, changes[]}` writes `releases/{id}` (server-side only) then pushes ONE notification + My Week feed item to every non-guest user via `notifyUsers()` (appKey `releases`, tag `release-v{version}`); GET = health probe the compose UI gates its send button on
  - `library.js` → `deletePaper` (HTTPS, V3.97): admin/uploader-gated cascade for removing a paper from RM's library — deletes the Cloud Storage PDF blob, recursive-deletes all `papers/{itemId}/*` subcollections (annotations, yjs_*, snapshots, comments, presence), scans every user's `userData/{uid}/tasks/*` to scrub `evidence.item_ids` references at every nested level (project/bucket/subtask/children), then deletes `items/{itemId}`. Bypasses storage.rules + firestore.rules via Admin SDK so client-side rules stay locked down. Idempotent — invokes on already-missing items still mop up orphan paper-tree subcollections.
- **Deployment:** `firebase deploy --only functions` (config in `firebase.json`)
- **Notification payload:** `{ notification: { title, body }, data: { title, body, url, tag }, webpush: { fcmOptions: { link } } }` — consumed by `firebase-messaging-sw.js`

### scripts/deploy.py + scripts/touch_folders.py (V3.817)

- **Entry points:** `python3 scripts/deploy.py [status|stage|ftp|verify|baseline|audit|touch-folders] [--only PREFIX] [--all] [--delete] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--no-keychain] [--force-all] [--purge-audit]`; `python3 scripts/touch_folders.py [--all | --hook | paths…]`.
- **State:** `deploy/site.json` (config, tracked), `deploy/manifest.json` (what is live, tracked), `deploy/pending.json` + `deploy/upload/` + `deploy/audit-*.txt` (transient, ignored). `DEPLOY_STATE_DIR` / `DEPLOY_SITE_JSON` env vars relocate state for tests.
- **Password for `ftp`:** `MCGHEELAB_FTP_PASSWORD` → macOS Keychain (`security find-internet-password -s host -a user -r "ftp " -w`, the entry Cyberduck saved) → prompt. Never stored by the script.
- **See** the V3.817 section at the top of this file.

### scripts/module_icons.py (V3.861)
- **Purpose:** gives a self-contained course module (modules/AUTHORING.md §0) the icons it uses without depending on `/rm/js/icons.js`: an inline sprite of exactly the referenced symbols, read from the generated `rm/js/icons.js` (one source of truth), plus `HI.svg(name, {solid, tint, label})` and `HI.draw(ctx, name, x, y, size, color)`.
- **Entry point:** `python3 scripts/module_icons.py <file…> | --all [--check]`. References it collects: `href="#hi-NAME[-solid]"`, `HI.svg('NAME'…)`, `HI.draw(ctx, 'NAME'…)`. Rewrites only the block between `<!-- hi-icons:start` and `<!-- hi-icons:end -->` (inserted after `<body>`); `--check` exits 1 on a stale block or an unknown name.

### scripts/build_extension_zip.py (V3.858)
- **Purpose:** builds the public Chrome-extension download, `rm/downloads/mcgheelab-capture-extension.zip`, from the unpacked source in the sibling `../ResearchManagement/extension/` (the extension still lives there; the site only ships the zip). Deterministic — sorted entries, fixed timestamps, fixed mode, `extension/` root folder — so `deploy/manifest.json`'s sha256 changes only when the extension's content does.
- **Entry point:** `python3 scripts/build_extension_zip.py [--src DIR] [--out FILE] [--check]`; `$MCGHEELAB_EXTENSION_DIR` overrides the source. `--check` exits 1 when the shipped zip is behind the source.
- **Never packed:** `key.pem` / any `*.pem` (would let the recipient publish updates as the PI), `.DS_Store`, `__pycache__/`, `.git/`, `test/`, `node_modules/` — the dev server route's list plus the fixtures.
- **Run it** after editing the extension; the zip then ships with the next deploy (`rm/**` is in `deploy/site.json`). The dev server's `/api/extension/download.zip` still rebuilds on the fly for local use, but the Library page's button serves the static file everywhere.

### scripts/release_push.py (V3.607)
- **Purpose:** Ships one batched release across BOTH surfaces — the web tree (FTP) and the Ourlab mobile app (TestFlight) — from a single input, `CodeLog/Updates/PENDING_RELEASE.md`. Exists because the phone app bundles `rm/` at build time, so an FTP-only push silently leaves app users on old code
- **Entry point:** `python3 scripts/release_push.py [--dry-run] [--verified] [--no-upload] [--web-only] [--force] [--version V] [--minor|--patch]`
- **Dependencies:** stdlib only. Needs `xcodebuild` / `xcrun altool`, the sibling `../OurlabMobile` repo, `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_UAZY3QKPQN.p8`, and the login-keychain distribution identity. ★ Must run OUTSIDE a sandbox (codesign → `errSecInternalComponent`)
- **Pipeline:** preflight (ledger entries + web version + 5-entry floor) → `bundled_web_diff()` (`diff -rq` app `public/rm` vs repo `rm`, pre-sync, `pages/*.html` filtered) → `bump_build` (both pbxproj blocks) → `write_mobile_changelog` (generated from the ledger, never hand-authored) → `npm run build` → device-verification gate → archive → export → `altool --upload-app` → `.last-release.json` baseline write → `roll_ledger` (pending → Shipped) → print the paste-ready announcement block
- **Version policy:** web version read from CHANGELOG head; mobile keeps its own `m-vX.Y.Z` line — patch for a bundle refresh, minor when hand-authored native files (`*.swift`, `Info.plist`, `*.entitlements`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `capacitor.config.json`, `package.json`, `scripts/*.mjs`, branding source) are **committed** since the baseline. Generated paths (`ios/App/App/public`, `Assets.xcassets`, `android/app/src/main/res`, `capacitor.build.gradle`) and `project.pbxproj` are excluded from the signal
- **State:** `../OurlabMobile/CodeLog/Updates/.last-release.json` — `{mobile_version, build, web_version, git_sha, date}`, written only after a successful upload
- **Not automated (deliberate):** the Cyberduck FTP (GUI-only) and pressing 📣 Send on `rm/pages/whats-new.html` (it notifies every lab member)

### scripts/slack_export.py
- **Purpose:** One-time Slack → Lab Chat history export run locally with admin Firebase credentials and a workspace-owner Slack user OAuth token. Built for the Slack-off-ramp transition; runs once (idempotent) per workspace, not as a live mirror
- **Entry point:** `python3 scripts/slack_export.py [--dry-run] [--channels …] [--skip-files] [--skip-dms]`
- **Dependencies:** `slack_sdk`, `firebase-admin`, `python-dotenv`, `requests` (see `scripts/requirements.txt`)
- **Config:** `scripts/.env` (template at `scripts/.env.example`); env vars `SLACK_USER_TOKEN`, `FIREBASE_SA_PATH`, `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `FIREBASE_BUCKET`, `IMPORTER_UID`. Both `.env` and the resume-state checkpoint `.slack_export_checkpoint.json` are gitignored
- **Schema additions** to existing Lab Chat collections:
  - `chatChannels/slack_{slackId}`: adds `importedFromSlack: true`, `slackChannelId`. Channels grouped under new `Slack archive` category appended to `chatConfig/settings.categories`
  - `chatMessages/{auto}`: adds `importedFromSlack: true`, `slackTs`, `slackChannelId`, `importedBy`. Idempotency check is a `where slackChannelId == X and slackTs == Y` query before each write
  - `users/slack_{slackId}` ghost docs for non-member Slack users: `imported: true`, `disabled: true`, `role: 'guest'` — gives messages a valid `authorUid` without enabling sign-in
- **Pipeline:** `fetch_all_users` → `fetch_all_channels` → `build_user_map` (email match against existing users, ghost-create otherwise) → for each channel: `ensure_channel_doc` → `fetch_history` (paginated, oldest→newest) → pass-1 writes top-level messages, pass-2 fetches `conversations.replies` for threads and writes with resolved `threadParentId`
- **Format conversion** (in `convert_text`): Slack `<@U…>` mentions resolve to `@displayname` and append to `mentions: [uid]`; `<#C…|name>` → `#name`; `<url|label>` → `label (url)`; `<!channel>`/`<!here>`/`<!everyone>` preserved as plain `@name` text but `mentionsChannel` forced false to suppress retroactive notification storms
- **Files:** downloaded from `url_private_download` with bearer auth, re-uploaded to Storage at `chat/imported/{slackChannelId}/{slackTs}_{name}` (made public to match other chat files); >50 MB skipped to honor `storage.rules` limit
- **Rate limiting & resume:** sleeps between Tier 3 calls and on `Retry-After` 429s; `.slack_export_checkpoint.json` records `channels_done` so re-runs skip completed channels (per-message dedup is via the `slackTs` query)
- **UI side:** `apps/chat/app.js` `renderMessageHTML()` adds a `chat-badge-imported` "from Slack" pill next to the timestamp when `msg.importedFromSlack === true`

### content.json
- **Purpose:** Static site content — mission, research, projects, team, classes
- **Role in V2.0:** Serves as baseline/fallback; Firestore user stories augment the projects page

### styles.css
- **Purpose:** Public site styling, responsive layout, animations
- **Responsive strategy:** Fluid typography via `clamp()`, auto-fit grids, breakpoints at 768px (tablet) and 600px (phone)

### user-styles.css
- **Purpose:** Styling for user system pages — auth forms, dashboard, story editor, admin panel, modals
- **Key patterns:** Form groups, status badges (draft/pending/published), section blocks, image upload zones, admin tables, tab navigation

### firestore.rules / storage.rules
- **Purpose:** Firebase security rules for Firestore and Storage
- **Access model:** Role-based (admin/editor/contributor); published stories and news posts readable by all; users write own profile; 10 MB image / 50 MB video upload limit; `newsPosts` collection follows same pattern as `stories`; `cvData` collection owner read/write + admin read; `cv/` storage path for BibTeX/PDF imports; `schedules` collection public read, owner/admin write (any authenticated user can create); `participants` collection public read, admin create/delete, self-update via auth UID or invite key; `classFiles` collection public read, auth create, admin update/delete; `classes/` storage path public read, auth write, 50 MB limit; `trackerData/{userId}` and `trackerEntries/{userId}/entries/{entryId}` strictly owner-only (no admin access) for activity tracker privacy; `meetings` collection authenticated read/create/update, admin-only delete; `meetingConfig` collection authenticated read, admin-only write; `equipment` collection authenticated read, admin-only write; `equipmentBookings` collection authenticated read/create, owner or admin update/delete; `equipmentTraining` collection authenticated read, admin-only write; `equipmentSettings` collection authenticated read, admin-only write; `chatConfig` collection authenticated read, admin-only write; `chatChannels` collection authenticated read/create/update, admin-only delete; `chatMessages` collection authenticated read/create, authenticated update (for reactions/read receipts), admin-only delete; `chatReadState` collection authenticated read/write; `chatUserMeta/{uid}` strictly owner-only

### DataIllustrations/ (interactive 3D data visualizations — V3.301)
- **Purpose:** Self-contained WebGL2 viewer pages surfaced on the public site at `#/data` (gallery) and `#/data/{vizId}?view={viewId}` (full viewer), and embedded as animated, non-interactive previews inside research-story/news sections
- **Registry:** `DataIllustrations/manifest.json` — `visualizations[]` of `{id, title, description, file, thumb, tags}`. Static file, FTP deploy (same pattern as `modules/manifest.json`). `id` is the stable key referenced by saved views and routes — never rename once views exist. Adding a viz = drop a new self-contained HTML viewer in this folder + one manifest entry. **All visualization folders are centralized here** — each viz is either a single HTML file at the DataIllustrations root or its own subfolder (e.g. `DataIllustrations/granular-flow/index.html`; folder-per-viz is the convention going forward since the collection will grow large). `file` accepts relative subpaths; `vizViewerUrl()` (app.js) sanitizes per-segment and drops `..`/`.` so Firestore-sourced values can never escape DataIllustrations/. `thumb` is a site-root-relative image path used as the gallery fallback poster when a viz has no saved views yet
- **viewer3d.html:** single-file raw-WebGL2 viewer (~4.3 MB; all data base64-embedded on one `const GEOM` line; zero external deps, opens from `file://`). Inline config API: `window.__getConfig()` → `{v:1, st, P, camera:{q, dist, target}}`; `window.__applyConfig(cfg)` (copies only known `st`/`P` keys, restores quaternion camera, rebuilds grain mesh, syncs HUD); `window.__snapshotBlob()` → PNG Blob; `?embed=1` hides all chrome and disables pointer input (`#cv{pointer-events:none}`); `#cfg=<base64 JSON>` applies a config before the first painted frame (re-applied on `hashchange`); `window.__setRunning()` + `visibilitychange` gate the rAF loop
- **Saved views:** Firestore `vizViews` collection — `{vizId, name, config, poster:{thumb,medium,full}, createdBy, createdByName, createdAt, updatedAt}`. Created from the full-viewer page by contributor+ (`isLabMember()` rule); posters go through `processImage()`/`uploadImageSet()` to Storage `vizViews/{viewDocId}/poster/`. DB methods in `user-system.js` use `where()`-only queries + client-side sort (no composite index)
- **Embeds:** story/news sections carry an optional denormalized `viz` field (`{vizId, viewId, name, file, poster, config}`) picked via `openVizPicker()`; `buildStoryHTML()` renders a `.viz-embed` poster + overlay link; `wireVizEmbeds()` (app.js) swaps in the live `?embed=1#cfg=` iframe when scrolled into view and removes it when it leaves (frees the WebGL context; browsers cap ~8–16/page; `MAX_LIVE_VIZ = 2`). Deleting a saved view never breaks published content (frozen copies); click-through to a deleted view opens the viewer at defaults
- **Extension point:** `projectPackages` could gain the same optional `viz` field rendered by `buildProjectExpandedHTML()` — no schema migration needed
- **SW note:** `viewer3d.html` is intentionally NOT in the sw.js precache shell; the HTTP cache dedupes the 4.3 MB fetch across embeds

### poster/
- **Purpose:** Standalone academic poster sub-site with its own Firebase integration

## Data Flow

### Public pages
```
URL hash change → app.js router → render from content.json → inject into #app
                                 → (async) fetch Firestore published stories → append to grid
```

### User system pages
```
URL hash change → app.js router → McgheeLab.render*() returns HTML string
               → inject into #app → McgheeLab.wire*() attaches event listeners
               → user actions → Firestore reads/writes → UI updates
```

### Authentication flow
```
Admin generates invitation → shares link → student opens #/login?token=...
  → validates token → creates Firebase Auth account → creates Firestore user profile
  → marks invitation used → redirects to #/dashboard
```

### CV builder flow
```
#/cv → wireCV() loads cvData from Firestore (or creates empty with profile pre-population)
  → user edits sections → persist() saves to Firestore + syncCVToProfile() updates user profile
  → imports: BibTeX/NSF/ORCID parsed into entries → DOI auto-fill via CrossRef
  → exports: LaTeX/BibTeX/PDF generated client-side → AI assistant calls Anthropic API with user's key
  → versioning: snapshots save visibility state per section/entry → can restore/compare
```

### Activity tracker flow (V3.327 — FuturePlan 04 Workstream B, hybrid model)
```
Two entry flavors in trackerEntries/{uid}/entries, both "activity", neither confirmed:
  MANUAL (source manual/ai): duration (minutes) + categoryPath = logged hours.
    Entered complete via the tracker's Daily view (hierarchical categories,
    Naive Bayes ML + Claude-API category suggestion, weekly analytics).
  AUTO (source rm-page-time / rm-notebook / rm-protocols / rm-paper-editor):
    kind:'work', categoryPath, NO duration = presence. Written with no confirm.
    - rm/js/page-time-tracker.js: any RM-page interaction marks the current
      10-min window → auto-pagetime-<slug>-<date> (logged_windows for
      cross-tab idempotency only).
    - rm/js/activity-signals.js: producers fire recordWork/recordSchedule
      (deterministic ids auto-<kind>-<id>[-<date>], idempotent).
Tracker (rm/js/activity-tracker.js) sidebar: Overview (heatmap + streaks +
  per-category counts over both flavors) · Daily (manual logging w/ hours) ·
  Weekly · Analytics · Categories · Settings. Restored from the V3.49 base
  after the V3.320 counts-only rewrite (the pre-rewrite rich version was lost
  to the V3.325 batch commit).
Hours are consistent everywhere: duration/60, bucketed by categoryPath[0].
  PMR Stats = hours by category + hours sparkline (+ V3.321 heatmap strip);
  lab-stats = hours table; dashboard = logged hours this week + streak.
  Auto events contribute 0 hours (presence only). shareActivity gate unchanged.
Note: the "hours are dead / counts only" stance of V3.319–V3.321 was reverted
  here per user direction; only page-time is fully automatic.
V3.329: the Daily view's suggestions come from the user's open TASKS
  (tasks/buckets.json → open subtasks assigned to them; "Log it" seeds a
  categorized entry), NOT from page activity — auto-presence entries
  (source rm-*) are excluded from the "uncategorized → categorize" prompt.
```

### Story creation flow
```
Dashboard → New Story → add sections (text + images/videos) → Save Draft / Publish / Submit
  → images auto-resized client-side → uploaded to Firebase Storage at 3 resolutions
  → videos (mp4/webm) uploaded directly to Firebase Storage (50 MB limit)
  → story saved to Firestore → status based on user role privileges
  → admin reviews pending stories → approve (published) or reject (back to draft)
```

## Design Decisions

- **No frameworks:** Keeps deployment simple, no build step needed
- **Hash routing:** Works with GitHub Pages and GoDaddy static hosting
- **JSON content store:** Enables non-developers to update text/team info without touching JS
- **Firebase backend:** Decoupled from hosting provider; free tier covers lab-scale usage
- **Compat SDK:** Firebase compat libraries work with vanilla JS script tags, no bundler needed
- **Client-side image resize:** Students upload one image; Canvas API generates thumb/medium/full as webp — simpler UX than asking for multiple files
- **Invitation-based registration:** Admin controls who can register; no open signups
- **Role-based publishing:** Admin sets user role → determines if stories auto-publish or need review
- **Graceful degradation:** Site works without Firebase configured; user system features simply hidden
- **Global namespace (`McgheeLab`):** User system modules communicate via `window.McgheeLab` to avoid ES module refactoring of the existing IIFE-based app.js

## PWA Architecture

### Service Workers
Two separate service workers coexist:
- **`sw.js`** — Caching service worker. Precaches shell (core HTML/CSS/JS) and all 8 lab app files on install. Runtime strategies: stale-while-revalidate (shell), cache-first (images/videos), network-first (CDN), network-only (Firebase API). Versioned caches enable clean updates.
- **`firebase-messaging-sw.js`** — FCM push notification handler. Receives background push messages, shows system notifications with vibration and desktop persistence, manages app icon badge counts via IndexedDB, handles notification clicks to navigate to relevant pages.

### Push Notification Flow
```
User grants permission → McgheePush.requestPermission(userId)
  → browser requests FCM token from Google → token returned
  → token stored in Firestore: users/{uid}/pushTokens/{token}
  → backend (Cloud Functions or admin) sends push via FCM Admin SDK
  → if app in foreground: onMessage callback → in-app toast
  → if app in background: firebase-messaging-sw.js → system notification
      → vibrate: [200, 100, 200] (Android)
      → requireInteraction: true (desktop — persists in tray)
      → tag: server-set or unique per message
      → badge count incremented via IndexedDB + Badging API
  → on notification click: clear badge, navigate to target URL
  → on app focus/visibility: clear badge via McgheePush.clearBadge()
```

### Push Permission Strategy
- **Standalone (installed PWA):** Native browser permission dialog fires proactively 1.5s after first auth resolve. `localStorage` flag `mcgheelab-push-prompted` prevents re-prompting.
- **Non-standalone (browser):** Passive "Enable notifications?" banner shown on Lab Apps hub page (`#/apps`). User must explicitly tap "Turn on".

### Badge Count Architecture
- **IndexedDB store:** `mcgheelab-badge` → key `count` — shared between service worker and main thread
- **Increment:** Service worker increments on each background push via `navigator.setAppBadge(count)`
- **Clear:** Main thread clears on `visibilitychange`/`focus` events and on initial load; service worker clears on `notificationclick`
- **Platform support:** Android Chrome PWA + desktop Chrome/Edge. Not supported on iOS.

### Installability
- **Android Chrome:** `beforeinstallprompt` event captured → custom "Install" button on apps hub
- **iOS Safari:** Detected via user agent → instructional banner ("Tap Share → Add to Home Screen")
- **Standalone mode:** `display-mode: standalone` CSS media query adjusts safe-area padding

### New Files
- `manifest.json` — Web app manifest (name, icons, shortcuts, display mode)
- `sw.js` — Caching service worker
- `firebase-messaging-sw.js` — Push notification service worker
- `push-notifications.js` — Client-side push permission/token management (`McgheePush` global)
- `icons/` — 13 icon PNGs at various sizes + maskable variant
- `favicon.ico` — Root favicon
